papers.title: Achieving high strength and high ductility in biodegradable Zn alloys
papers.abstract: Simultaneously improving strength and ductility remains a critical challenge for biodegradable Zn alloys. Here, we demonstrate that a Zn-0.5Mg-0.2Mn-0.2Al-0.2Cu-0.02Li alloy, processed by multi-component microalloying followed by 4-pass equal-channel angular pressing (ECAP) via route BC, achieves an exceptional strength-ductility synergy. Microalloying supplies solute atoms and Mg2Zn11, Al11Mn4 and Al10MnZn89 particle populations that strengthen the matrix and regulate boundary migration. ECAP subsequently refines the mean grain size from 1.74 to 1.43 μm, fragments the coarse Mg2Zn11 and Al11Mn4 constituents, and redistributes the finer particles. This coupled microstructural regulation produces a yield strength of 327 ± 4.2 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 395 ± 2.8 MPa, and an elongation of 82.8 ± 3.5%, representing increases of 16.4%, 13.5%, and 88.6%, respectively, relative to the as-extruded condition. Quantitative strengthening analysis reveals that grain boundary strengthening, particle strengthening, and dislocation hardening all contribute to the high strength, while the exceptional ductility is primarily attributed to particle fragmentation and dynamic recrystallization during tensile deformation. Visco-Plastic Self-Consistent (VPSC) analysis further suggests that coordinated basal and non-basal slip provides a secondary contribution to the enhanced plasticity. Beyond mechanical performance, ECAP reduces the degradation rate in simulated body fluid by 36% (from 0.359 to 0.230 mm year-1), while the alloy exhibits an antibacterial rate of 99.1% and a hemolysis ratio of 1.93%. Long-term in vivo evaluation at 24 weeks indicates favorable systemic biocompatibility, normal hepatorenal function, and superior osseointegration. These results indicate that microalloying establishes a strengthened, particle-containing matrix, while ECAP optimizes its grain and particle architecture, enabling concurrent improvements in mechanical performance, degradation uniformity, and bone integration.

papers.title: Agentic AI for Intent Management and Control in Autonomous Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automation will help future mobile networks translate high-level network intents into concrete network optimization or control actions. However, existing approaches often focus on intent management and orchestration, leaving the adaptation of underlying network optimization and control functions largely unaddressed. This article proposes a triadic agentic AI framework that co-designs intent management and intent fulfillment through three agents: an interpreter, powered by a language model, that translates and refines intents into machine-readable optimization templates; an optimizer that adapts controller policies to intent specifications; and a controller that performs fast decision-making. We discuss the design space of each agent and how the workflow can be embedded across network architectural domains. Finally, we develop a concrete realization combining a language-model interpreter with Bayesian optimization for the optimizer and multi-objective reinforcement learning for the controller, and evaluate it in a radio resource management case study for differentiated connectivity. Results demonstrate how the agentic AI framework can connect high-level intents with runtime network control, showing adaptability of intent specifications and control policies to service requirements and changing network conditions.

papers.title: Generalizing Agentic Robotics via Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Building general-purpose robots is a central goal in robotics. Agentic robotics pursues this goal with planners that control robots through tool calls. However, existing methods either rely on proprietary models accessed through APIs, which incur high costs and latency, or post-train a planner with reinforcement learning (RL) in a single domain, requiring a separate specialist for each domain with incompatible tools. In large language model (LLM) post-training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) has been used to consolidate domain specialists into a single generalist. Yet whether MOPD can build a generalist planner for agentic robotics, how well it performs, and how it compares with other consolidation methods remain unexplored. In this paper, we systematically study these questions: we introduce Robo-MOPD, which trains a single student on closed-loop rollouts in simulation under token-level supervision from matching frozen specialists, and compare it with weight merging, off-policy specialist supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and multi-domain online RL. Experiments on LIBERO-PRO and RoboCasa365 show that a single 9B Robo-MOPD planner reaches 72.9% and 44.8% success (58.9% average), surpassing all consolidated baselines in average success and both 9B specialists on their respective benchmarks. Robo-MOPD excels on long-horizon tasks, outperforming multi-domain online RL by 13.0 percentage points on LIBERO-10.

papers.title: DexLatentWorld: 3D Cross-Embodiment Latent Action World Models for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: World models facilitate planning and control in robotic manipulation by enabling agents to anticipate the consequences of their actions. However, they typically rely on action-labelled interaction data that is costly to acquire and difficult to scale. These models are also often tied to the specific embodiment they were trained on, limiting transferability to previously unseen robot morphologies. We introduce a 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations directly from point-cloud observations of retargeted human manipulation demonstrations. A contrastive objective is used to encourage consistent representations of motion across embodiments. The resulting unified latent action space serves directly as the search space for model-predictive control, where sampled latent actions condition particle-based future predictions. Executable robot commands are then recovered from the predicted geometric motion without requiring an embodiment-specific action decoder. Through extensive evaluations, we demonstrate that the learned latent actions exhibit controllable and compositional motion, transfer to unseen robot embodiments, and support zero-shot manipulation with unseen gripper geometries. Following task-agnostic adaptation, our model achieves 90%, 92%, and 60% success on reaching, grasping, and placing, respectively, compared with DexWM's reported 72%, 58%, and 28%. Finally, we demonstrate zero-shot real-world manipulation with an unseen dexterous hand, achieving an 86% success rate across 50 trials on five diverse tasks involving pushing, grasping, and lifting everyday objects. These results highlight the potential of geometry-grounded latent actions as a unified, transferable interface for world-model-based robotic manipulation. Project materials, including demonstration videos and source code, are available at https://vinaymohan0409.github.io/DexLatentWorld/.

papers.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
papers.abstract: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. Viewing the world model as a LAM, we show that these dynamics can be extracted with minimal changes to the model. Native LAM operates one pretrained video diffusion transformer as both IDM and FDM, with learnable dynamics registers as the only causal bridge between the two, and trains on counterfactual temporal pairs that differ in motion alone, so that the registers distill a video's dynamics into a compact native latent action. We further propose a pretraining paradigm for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, Pretraining Actions from World models (PAWlicy), in which Native LAM serves as a dynamics teacher on large-scale video; unlike world action models, it never generates video. Native latent actions outperform existing LAMs on the LARY benchmark in both action classification and control regression, and replay the same motion on new robots, in new scenes, and from human hands to robots, although no transfer objective is used in training. With a 3.8B model, PAWlicy reaches a 93.6% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 trained with domain-randomized demonstrations, the highest among VLAs. On RoboDojo, it is competitive on every dimension we evaluate, and its Precision, evaluated by us, is on par with the leading leaderboard entries. On real robots, it improves over the pi_0.5 baseline on both tasks. Both stages use only public data and a publicly released world model.

papers.title: Can Multimodal Fusion MakeSense for Embodied Vision in Degraded Sensing?
papers.abstract: Embodied vision systems rely on complementary sensors to perceive and act as conditions change. Even models that accept arbitrary sensor subsets can exhibit negative fusion: adding a sensor increases prediction error. We propose MakeSense, a multimodal fusion framework that preserves sensor-specific evidence in private streams and combines information through shared bottleneck tokens. Training pairs full and subset views of the same degraded observations, penalizing higher error with more sensors. Where geometry permits, the distance readout uses range measurements alone, while the rest of the prediction draws on all available inputs. Paired tests across five datasets reveal helpful and harmful sensor additions. MakeSense reduces negative fusion on MM-Fi. With lightweight adapters and per-dataset training, the same design improves UAV localization on MMAUD, cooperative 3D detection on V2X-Real, few-shot pose transfer to RELI11D, and command prediction on Humanoid-Everyday, where a world model trained on the frozen core's outputs forecasts future fused states more accurately than a linear baseline at longer tested horizons. MakeSense supports embodied sensing across human activity, aerial systems, robotics, and autonomous driving.

papers.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

papers.title: SignalCount: Approximate Counts with Structured and Semantic Predicates in Seconds
papers.abstract: Many applications store records with structured columns and a text document, and ask how many records in a filtered set meet a criterion that only a reader of the text can judge, such as "How many patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 40 to 70, stopped metformin because their blood sugar stayed high?" An interactive application needs this count in seconds, as the user types the criterion, to decide whether the matching set is worth materializing with a batch pipeline in which an LLM judges the records. Prior approximate query processing over such semantic predicates has an expensive model, the oracle, label a sample at query time, so every query waits for the oracle. We present SignalCount, a production system that answers COUNT queries with structured and semantic predicates and calls no oracle at query time, even for ad-hoc criteria. Its oracle is the production LLM judge, and the judge's logged verdicts calibrate, offline, the fast classifier that already runs in front of the judge. At query time, SignalCount counts the filtered set exactly and draws a uniform sample of at most 1,000 records in one columnar scan, scores the sample with the classifier, and multiplies the average calibrated probability by the exact count. Its 90% interval combines a sampling term with one-sided, rate-dependent margins for calibration error, fitted by split conformal prediction across tenants. In a multi-tenant production deployment, latency has a p99 of 3.8 s and stays flat as the filtered set grows beyond the sample. On tenants held out from fitting, the interval covers the count that the production pipeline returns in 92% of estimates, although estimates run about 15% high in aggregate, because a calibration nearly unbiased per record is still biased per criterion.

papers.title: Beyond the Black Box: A Diagnosis-Driven Agent for Interpretable MIP Solver Tuning
papers.abstract: Tuning a mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver is an instance-specific problem, where a poor configuration can increase solving time by orders of magnitude.   Existing Bayesian optimization tuners treat solver tuning as a black-box optimization problem: each evaluation returns a single score, allowing the tuner to learn which configuration is faster, but not why.   Inspired by the use of profilers in GPU-kernel optimization, we introduce APEC (Agent for Per-instance Explainable Configuration), a log-grounded tuning agent for MIP solvers.   APEC has three layers: a deterministic layer that profiles each log, an interpretation layer that guides hypothesis-driven diagnosis, and a system layer that controls evaluation, enabling more reliable and interpretable solver tuning.   On the full MIPLIB 2017 benchmark set, APEC achieves a 1.58X improvement over the default configuration with over 38% fewer parameter changes than the baselines, making the results easier to read.

papers.title: Zhengrong: World Models with Pole-Based Action-Response Factorization for Direct Visual Planning
papers.abstract: Direct visual world models predict the effects of candidate action sequences without recursive latent rollout, yet they leave the temporal structure of action effects unspecified. We introduce Zhengrong (Zhengrong-PoleWM), a world model that decomposes a latent trajectory into an initial-condition anchor, a free response, and delayed responses to action innovations. Nonlinear networks map visual history and causal action prefixes to response coefficients. A shared bank of stable conjugate poles determines how each response evolves with elapsed time. This factorization preserves nonlinear interactions across actions, anchors predictions exactly at the initial state, prevents future actions from affecting earlier predictions, and yields bounded responses to finite control plans. We derive an exact re-anchoring identity that identifies the additional basis direction $Ψ_κ(s)$ needed to represent shifted trajectory tails. Across four offline image-goal control benchmarks (Cube, TwoRoom, PushT, and Reacher), Zhengrong-PoleWM achieves $90.83\% \pm 0.47\%$ macro-average success over two training seeds at epoch 20, exceeding the strongest baseline (QQWorld) by 6.08 percentage points. Selecting checkpoints by validation loss yields $91.21\% \pm 1.00\%$. In a controlled first-epoch Cube study without restart regularization, neural and pole response heads outperform a generic direct predictor by 20.67 and 23.34 percentage points, respectively. On an NVIDIA A100 GPU, median latency for a full 30-iteration cross-entropy method search ranges from 74 to 87 ms across the four tasks. The mean of these medians is 77.5 ms, a 15.8% latency reduction relative to Fast-LeWM and a $7.1\times$ speedup over autoregressive LeWM.

papers.abstract: Learning how actions change visual states is essential for prediction and decision-making in embodied tasks. ActField separates action-independent evolution from action-induced changes, with the latter modulated by the latent context. A reference-conditioned representation and multi-step dynamics loss further support accurate long-horizon prediction. Together, these components provide a structured and temporally continuous formulation for predicting action-conditioned visual dynamics. Experiments across LIBERO, DROID, and BEHAVIOR demonstrate improved visual prediction fidelity and more accurate action-induced motion prediction over existing world models. Further evaluations on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the utility of ActField in improving downstream policy planning through VLM-guided action selection.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization for Inhomogeneous Functions via Locally Adaptive Kernels
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. However, many complex real-world functions have highly inhomogeneous regularity, exhibiting both smooth and rough behavior. This fundamental mismatch between the model and the black-box function severely degrades both sample efficiency and surrogate accuracy of BO. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Inhomogeneous Bayesian optimization framework. We develop a partitioned modeling strategy that dynamically subdivides the search space into subdomains, capturing spatially varying smoothness through locally adaptive kernels. To dynamically adjust the spatial resolution of the surrogate model, this approach utilizes a recursive splitting criterion. Furthermore, we develop a sampling allocation theory, establishing that driving the regional acquisition suprema below a common target level is achieved by polynomially denser sampling in rougher subdomains. Numerical experiments across homogeneous functions, synthetic inhomogeneous functions, and a real-world 8-dimensional LASSO hyperparameter tuning task demonstrate that our approach improves optimization efficiency on synthetic inhomogeneous functions, while performing comparably to Classic BO on homogeneous functions and on the LASSO task. This demonstrates the robustness of the adaptive partitioning mechanism.

papers.title: Write, Evolve, Read: Streaming Cameras into a Persistent World State for 4D Occupancy Forecasting
papers.abstract: 4D occupancy forecasting predicts the 3D semantic occupancy of a driving scene seconds ahead. Over a few seconds, the scene changes little while the vehicle moves, so most of the space ahead has already been seen. Sorting the future into unchanged, changed, and unseen space, we find that current camera-based world models fall short on the unchanged part: they fail to hold on to what they have already seen, rather than to forecast what will change. We therefore make what the model has seen its state. PersistWorld streams camera frames into a persistent 3D world state anchored in the scene, writing each frame once instead of rebuilding the state from past frames. The state is learned end to end with the forecast, and an evolver predicts it at any queried time along the ego trajectory. On Occ3D-nuScenes, PersistWorld raises the IoU of the best camera-based world model by 19 points at 1-3 s and by 18 to 24 points up to 8 s, while running more than twice as fast. papers.title: VeriTouch: Verified Visuo-Tactile World Models that Improve Robot Policy Learning
papers.abstract: Scaling visuo-tactile policy learning is constrained by the high cost of real-world data collection and the difficulty of building realistic simulations. Generative models offer a scalable source of training data, yet useful demonstrations require plausible tactile feedback, temporal alignment with visual contact, and accurate actions. To this end, we present VeriTouch, a framework for generating and verifying synthetic visuo-tactile trajectories for policy learning. Conditioned on initial images and task instructions, our world model, VeriGen, jointly generates high-fidelity dual-view videos and realistic tactile sequences over complete manipulation trajectories. By integrating a dedicated tactile expert with a pretrained video model, it captures realistic visual details and tactile deformation dynamics through joint visuo-tactile modeling. Our multimodal verifier VeriEval then checks visual quality while focusing on tactile reliability, assessing tactile realism, contact-force plausibility, and temporal alignment between visible contact and tactile signals, thereby directly filtering out unreliable sequences. Finally, our inverse dynamics model, VeriIDM, combines global scene information from both camera views with fine-grained gripper details and motion across neighboring frames to extract actions from verified videos. Experiments on five real-world tasks show that synthetic data improves all four evaluated policies, with further scaling synthetic trajectories substantially boosting policy performance without additional real-world data collection.

papers.abstract: Automated verification of industrial assembly processes remains a challenging problem due to substantial visual variability, limited availability of labeled defect data, and the fine-grained nature of many assembly errors. Existing approaches often rely on object detection, CAD models, or supervised classification pipelines, which can struggle to generalize across changing products and assembly configurations. In this work, we propose a novel self-supervised assembly verification framework based on Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs). Starting from the JEPA-based world model LeWorldModel, we investigate how the architecture must be adapted to verify the correctness of fine-grained assembly operations. To this end, we formulate assembly verification as a predictive world modeling task operating on before-and-after observations of assembly processes. Experimental results on industrial assembly tasks demonstrate that the proposed approach reliably detects both fine-grained incorrect assembly states and action-state mismatches, achieving an AUROC of 86.9% on a newly introduced assembly verification dataset. These results indicate that JEPA-based predictive representations constitute a promising foundation for robust and data-efficient industrial assembly verification.

papers.title: Autonomous UAV Navigation in an Unknown Environment via Multi-Trajectory Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: A novel model predictive control (MPC) formulation, named multi-trajectory MPC (mt-MPC), is presented and applied to the problem of autonomous navigation of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in an unknown environment. The UAV is equipped with a LiDAR sensor, providing only a partial description of the surroundings and resulting in time-varying constraints as the vehicle navigates among the obstacles. The control system layout is hierarchical: the low-level loops stabilize the vehicle's trajectories and track the set-points commanded by the high-level, mt-MPC controller. The latter is required to plan the UAV trajectory trading off safety, i.e. to avoid collisions with the uncertain obstacles, and exploitation, i.e. to reach an assigned target location. To achieve this goal, mt-MPC considers different future state trajectories in the same Finite Horizon Optimal Control Problem (FHOCP), enabling a partial decoupling between constraint satisfaction (safety) and cost function minimization (exploitation). Recursive feasibility and, consequently, persistent obstacle avoidance guarantees are derived under the assumption of a time invariant environment. The performance of the approach is studied in simulation and compared with that of a standard MPC, showing good improvement.

papers.title: Does coverage explain core-set active learning? Mean, max, and the choice of distance
papers.abstract: Core-set selection casts batch active learning as a covering problem, in which the points to label minimise the covering radius of the pool. Its main argument is a generalization bound in which this radius controls the gap between the loss on the pool and on the labelled sample. We examine what this bound requires and what it says in practice. We first state it with the assumption that its proof uses at the labelled points, a zero conditional risk, and show that it then holds for any dissimilarity and any selection rule that uses no label outside the sample. The proof works point by point and involves two averages, the mean distance of the pool to the labelled sample and the purity of the cells attached to the labelled points. Keeping them gives, when labels are deterministic at the labelled points, a bound on the pool loss with no zero-loss assumption and without the factor C, the number of classes, of the original constant. We then compare scales, for deterministic labels and a regression function Lipschitz on the whole pool. With the original constant, the bound can be informative only if the radius is below the smallest distance between two classes divided by C. Without C, its radius form can be informative only once the nearest-neighbour rule built on the sample is exact on the pool. Finally, a misalignment criterion measures whether a quantity ranks selections as the gap or the test error do. Experiments on a Gaussian pool and on two image pools, digits and MNIST, the latter under eight distances, and with a network retrained at each cycle, show that the radius does not rank selections consistently with the gap and, on the image pools, that the bounds that do not use the labels of the pool are never informative and that covering in mean rather than in maximum, as greedy k-medoids does, gives a higher purity and accuracy than random sampling.

papers.title: IP-GNO: An Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator for Automated Distribution System State Estimation
papers.abstract: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is a crucial tool for real-time monitoring, operation, and control of the new-age distribution systems (DSs) due to intensified voltage fluctuations and operational uncertainties introduced by volatile power injection at the nodes. Existing GNN-based approaches generally exhibit limited generalization across networks with different sizes and topologies, making zero-shot cross-grid transfer to unseen DSs a significant challenge. To overcome the aforementioned challenges, this article proposes an Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator (IP-GNO) for scalable and transferable DSSE. The proposed framework frames complex bus voltage estimation as an operator-learning problem inspired by the Neumann series expansion of the inverse bus admittance matrix. An admittance-parameterized kernel, incorporating a self-admittance gate in the zeroth-order term and a persistent source-injection skip connection across network layers, captures the underlying electrical dependencies. Additionally, a Physics-Embedded Tree Encoding (PETE) scheme introduces five grid-size-invariant positional features derived from path impedance and a DC-linearized phase-angle prior. A sine-cosine output formulation is further employed to address phase-angle periodicity and ensure stable training. The proposed IP-GNO module is evaluated on two small (IEEE 33- and 69-bus), two medium (IEEE 123- and 136-bus), and one large (2522-bus) sized DSs. Particularly, its zero-shot cross-grid generalization capability is investigated by training the model exclusively on the IEEE 33-bus system and directly evaluating it on four unseen distribution networks of different sizes without retraining or fine-tuning. A detailed comparative analysis with the existing state-of-the-art DSSE tools proves the superiority of IP-GNO, enabling scalable DSSE across heterogeneous DSs.

Since an incorrect motion can injure the patient, developing and evaluating these systems calls for a world model of colonoscopy. Such a model must follow a commanded scope motion, keep the colon anatomy consistent, and show lesions and procedural events. Yet camera-controlled generators trained on general scenes lose the colon's structure under motion, and endoscopic generators offer no camera control. We present ColonoWorld, a colonoscopy world model conditioned on a camera trajectory and a coarse 3D tube of the colon, trained on in vivo videos. From a whole-colon tube, it generates a full cecum-to-rectum procedure, even for unseen colon shapes. It also places polyps, instruments, and irrigation at specified locations and times. ColonoWorld outperforms state-of-the-art video generators, reducing camera trajectory error by 32% and FVD by 29%. Our code and annotations will be released at https://aidaslab.github.io/ColonoWorld.

papers.title: FMSNO: Scaling Surface Neural Operators by Learned Flow Matching Reparametrisation
papers.abstract: We propose the Flow Matching Surface Neural Operator (FMSNO), which combines learning a shared map from irregular surface meshes to a regular two-dimensional grid on the sphere and training a neural operator on the regular grid. Constructing a separate map for each new geometry can dominate inference time on large meshes. We initially pretrain the mapping by flow matching using precomputed optimal transport maps as targets and then continue its training using combined geometry and CFD objectives. We apply it to unseen geometries in a single forward pass. The learned flow deforms the surface points, and we project its endpoints onto the sphere. We then splat geometric features onto the spherical grid, apply a neural operator (we tested both Fourier and Spherical Fourier Neural Operators), and interpolate its output back to the surface. For a mesh with $N$ points, evaluating the map costs O(N), and the full prediction costs O(NlogN) with the FNO backbone. We evaluate surface pressure prediction on ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, and drag coefficient prediction on DrivAerNet++. Across the three pressure benchmarks, our accuracy is on par with that of the most accurate baseline. On a surface with one million points, our method achieves a 354x end-to-end inference speedup over that baseline while keeping the same memory usage asymptotics of O(N).

papers.abstract: Multi-robot embodied systems are typically designed to collaborate by coordinating actions, sharing trajectories, or learning joint policies. We ask a complementary question: can collaboration emerge before decision-making, by first building a shared understanding of the environment? We introduce Shared Environmental Understanding, a policy-agnostic representation that aggregates partial egocentric observations from multiple robots into a shared latent world model. This shifts collaboration from the policy space to the representation space, enabling decentralized decision-making with shared environmental context. To this end, we propose Shared Environment Encoding and Retrieval (SEER), a framework that organizes multi-robot observations into a shared memory, retrieves relevant context via spatio-temporal similarity, and encodes it using a predictive latent world model. The resulting representations are injected into downstream navigation agents as tokens. Experimental results demonstrate that SEER captures action-relevant environmental structure and consistently improves navigation performance across both specialized VLN agents and general vision-language model agents, while preserving single-agent capabilities.

papers.title: Topology-Prior-Guided Regional Latent Dynamics for Transient Structural Response Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting the transient nonlinear responses of complex engineering structures remains challenging due to large finite element meshes, heterogeneous structural components, and history-dependent mechanical behavior. This study proposes a topology-prior-guided regional latent dynamics (TPLD) surrogate model that combines physically structured regional representations with dynamics-aware latent learning for full-field time-history prediction. Based on mesh topology and engineering priors, structural responses are encoded into spatially coupled regional latent variables through region-aware feature extraction and topology-constrained interactions. An auxiliary one-step prediction task enhances latent-space dynamical predictability by introducing state-transition supervision. A load-conditioned spatiotemporal Mamba model then predicts regional latent trajectories by integrating temporal causal scanning and bidirectional spatial scanning, while a shared coordinate-conditioned decoder reconstructs full-field nodal responses. The framework is evaluated on three finite element datasets: a parametric stiffened panel, a partitioned pressure impact plate, and a Toyota Yaris full-vehicle crash model. The relative L2 errors for the three displacement components range from 4.00% to 8.21% on the stiffened panel and from 1.41% to 12.22% on the approximately 1.49-million-node vehicle model. On the BIW crash benchmark, TPLD achieves a relative L2 position error of 0.620%, representing a 30.7% reduction compared with the best-performing GeoTransolver configuration. Ablation studies demonstrate the advantages of topology-guided regional representations over global latent and learnable soft-slice alternatives, while auxiliary one-step prediction particularly improves the prediction of accumulated plastic strain.

papers.title: MASTO: Missed-thrust Aware Stochastic Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Missed Thrust Events (MTEs) are a major roadblock towards widespread adoption of low-thrust propulsion for deep space missions. Unplanned thruster outages have previously been difficult to directly incorporate in the preliminary mission design process, and current approaches mostly introduce robustness by conservative heuristics such as mandatory coasting arcs, which do not possess any safety guarantees, and usually only consider one missed-thrust event. Therefore, in this work, we utilize a stochastic hybrid system framework to model a spacecraft as a Markov jump system that can switch between nominal and failure mode. We formulate the Missed-thrust resilient trajectory optimization problem as a Markov jump covariance steering problem, and propose a sequential convex programming-based approach, which can also respect chance constraints. We demonstrate our framework on two complex three-dimensional transfers in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three body problem, showcasing robustness against a range of MTEs, while respecting chance constraints. We further analyze controller performance across a range of MTE-probability distributions, offering valuable insights into the MTE-resilient trajectory design trade space.

papers.title: IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. Practical simulations span a range of $\varepsilon$, so a single model covering this range is needed. PDE-specific neural operators are accurate but must be retrained at every $\varepsilon$; general neural operators cover $\varepsilon$ in one model but lose the phase-field structure of the target. We introduce Interface-Augmented Diffusion-Reaction (IADR), a neural operator that addresses both shortcomings: a target network with a diffusion-and-reaction (DR) structure preserves the phase-field structure of the Allen-Cahn equation, while a hypernetwork that maps $\varepsilon$ to the weights of this target network amortises the dependence on $\varepsilon$ across the range. A single IADR matches the per-$\varepsilon$ specialists on in-distribution data within the prescribed range, retains their cross-shape generalisation under both $\varepsilon$- and geometry-out-of-distribution shifts, and retains their compact DR target structure with millisecond-scale inference. We further establish a conditional $K$-step rollout error bound under consistency and stability assumptions.

papers.title: PushMimic: Learning Adaptive Humanoid Box Pushing via Dynamic Motion Augmentation and Reference Distillation
papers.abstract: Humanoid box pushing is challenging when the physical properties of the task, such as the box mass and the ramp inclination, are unknown before the push begins. This paper presents PushMimic, a framework that learns adaptive humanoid box pushing from a single level-ground kinematic reference motion. The learned policy adapts its pushing posture to these properties without observing them. PushMimic augments the reference motion into a dynamically feasible motion dataset over these properties with sampling-based trajectory optimization, and distills the dataset into one motion tracking policy in one stage of training. Simulation results over box masses from 5 to 15 kg and ramp inclinations up to 15 degrees show that PushMimic raises the success rate from 57.8% to 88.8% compared with a baseline that tracks the original reference motion. It also reduces the cost of push of the arms by 22%. Hardware experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid show that the policy adapts its torso pitch during continuous pushing on an inclined treadmill, with box masses up to 19 kg and ramp inclinations up to 12.6 degrees. PushMimic therefore needs only one reference motion, instead of one for every box mass and ramp inclination.

papers.title: One Latent World for Heterogeneous LiDARs: A Scan Pattern Agnostic 4D World Model via Direct Ray Decoding
papers.abstract: LiDAR world models generate and predict metric 3D observations in the form of LiDAR scans. They typically synthesize scans following the scan pattern of their training sensor or render them from an intermediate 3D surface or field. However, following one scan pattern limits transfer to LiDARs with other patterns, and rendering from intermediate geometry can cause incorrect depths and false returns. In this paper, we propose a scan pattern agnostic 4D LiDAR world model that decouples the scene from sensor observation, so one spatial latent can be observed by heterogeneous LiDARs at the same mounting position without regeneration. Our decoder predicts the hit probability and depth of each ray directly from the latent, combining global scene context with local features retrieved at a preliminary depth. Without an intermediate surface or field, it reduces incorrect depths and false returns, and as each ray is decoded independently from one latent, LiDARs that share a ray receive the same return and observe one consistent scene. Finally, a diffusion transformer generates scenes in this latent and predicts 4D sequences from observed latents warped by the given ego and object motion. On KITTI-360 and nuScenes, our model generates realistic scenes and reduces the registration error between predicted frames by about 70% relative to the best compared world model. Its decoder yields 19 to 28% lower depth error than the rendering used by other world models, and generated scans benefit several downstream tasks. Our code will be open-sourced. More details are available at https://minwoo0611.github.io/OneLatentWorld.

papers.title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming
papers.abstract: Terraforming Mars is a long-horizon, action-conditioned control problem that requires predicting atmospheric responses to interventions over centuries to identify effective policies. This position paper argues that physics-regularized recurrent state-space world models are the most promising foundation for this setting. Data-driven climate emulators lack action-conditioning, and physics-based general circulation models (GCMs) are too expensive for policy search. Among learned world models, recurrent state-space architectures with physics constraints are better suited than transformer-based alternatives: they provide native uncertainty quantification through their stochastic-deterministic decomposition, remain stable under sparse non-terrestrial training data, and enforce physical consistency at each rollout step. To make this position concrete, we describe a potential architecture combining JEPA-inspired latent encoding, universal differential equation constraints, and a Dreamer-lineage planning head. We also introduce MarsWorld, an open benchmark proposal for intervention-conditioned planetary world models, and discuss broader implications and objections.

papers.title: Compute-Efficient 2.5D Deep Learning for Morphology-Aware Porosity Segmentation in LPBF CoCr XCT Images
papers.abstract: X-ray computed tomography (XCT) is widely used for internal porosity inspection in laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) components, but accurate defect segmentation often relies on computationally expensive 3D deep learning models that are difficult to deploy in practical manufacturing environments. This study proposes a compute-efficient 2.5D deep learning framework for morphology-aware porosity segmentation in LPBF CoCr XCT images. The method stacks adjacent XCT slices as multi-channel inputs to a lightweight encoder–decoder U-Net, capturing local inter-slice pore continuity while retaining the low memory demand and fast inference of slice-based networks; an ablation over the context window confirms that one neighboring slice on each side (k=1) gives the best accuracy–efficiency trade-off. Beyond pixel-wise segmentation, a morphology-aware module extracts pore descriptors equivalent diameter, aspect ratio, circularity, solidity, elongation, and layer-wise porosity for engineering-relevant defect characterization. On the public NIST CoCr dataset, the 2.5D model attains IoU 0.941 and Dice 0.969 on the most porous held-out sample (72% porosity) at 11 ms per slice and 2.1 GB GPU memory, a 13–26× inference speedup over 3D baselines. Leave-one-sample-out cross-validation confirms this advantage is consistent across the full 1.37–72% porosity range (mean IoU 0.939±0.008). The model also yields the highest correlation with ground-truth morphology, including equivalent diameter (r=0.953) and layer-wise porosity fraction (r=0.985), while preserving bimodal pore-size distributions. The framework offers a compact, scalable solution for XCT-driven quality assurance in metal additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Quasi-static mechanical properties of AlSi10Mg menger sponge fractal structures fabricated by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: With the increasing demand for engineering protection and equipment weight reduction, the research and development of lightweight and high-energy-absorbing structures is becoming increasingly urgent. The Menger sponge fractal structure, through its self-similar hierarchical configuration, undergoes multi-stage crushing and is one of the ideal topologies for achieving the coordinated regulation of stiffness and energy absorption. To reveal the influence of fractal order on the compression mechanical behavior and energy absorption characteristics of the Menger sponge fractal structures (MFCs), in this experiment, multi-order MFC specimens of AlSi10Mg were prepared using SLM. After tensile calibration of the same batch of substrate, quasi-static compression, DIC observation and finite element simulation were carried out. The results show that with a fractal dimension of FD = 2.727, the MFC specimens exhibit typical hierarchical crushing and multi-stage plateau characteristics. Strain localization begins at the edge of the aperture and is transmitted layer by layer along the secondary rods. With the increase of order, the initial stiffness decreases from 133.03 kN/mm to 46.97 kN/mm, and the equivalent elastic modulus decreases from 4.93 GPa to 1.74 GPa. The equivalent modulus and the elastic limit decay power-law with relative density. The decay is caused by the coupling of four mechanisms: geometric dilution, bending dominant deformation, stress concentration at the hole edge, and forming defects. The specific energy absorption shows a pattern of first increasing and then decreasing. The specific energy absorption of the second-order MFC is the best (60.32 J/g, which is 65.2% higher than that of the first order). Through experiments and simulations, the optimal order is the second order. The above results provide a reference for the order design and material-process selection of metal fractal energy-absorbing structures for protective engineering.

papers.abstract: Maxillary sinus lifting is a surgical procedure widely used in dentistry to enable oral rehabilitation with dental implants in the posterior maxilla, particularly in cases involving bone loss or pneumatization of the maxillary sinus. The procedure aims to increase the available bone height for implant placement, thereby promoting greater stability and successful osseointegration. Notable techniques for maxillary sinus lifting include the Summers technique and the lateral window technique—developed by Dr. Hilt Tatum in 1974—which is indicated primarily for cases with significant bone deficiency. This study aimed to describe the main maxillary sinus lifting techniques and the importance of proper planning through a literature review. Regarding materials and methods, this is an exploratory bibliographic study based on searches in the Scientific Electronic Library Online (SciELO), Virtual Health Library (VHL/BVS), and Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS) databases; scientific articles, theses, books, journals, and dissertations served as sources. It is concluded that maxillary sinus lifting techniques are fundamental for achieving bone gain during dental implant rehabilitation in the posterior maxilla. Achieving satisfactory results requires a thorough patient history (anamnesis), detailed surgical planning, the selection of high-quality biomaterials, and patient follow-up; these factors contribute to a better prognosis and treatment success.

papers.abstract: A method is proposed to quantify resistance and define system failure of steel girder bridges that is suitable for reliability-based design optimization (RBDO) under blast events. The approach considers the ability of the structure to support vehicular traffic for temporary or emergency use post-blast. The method is demonstrated by minimizing the cost of a typical steel girder bridge while providing a given level of reliability. Uncertainties in critical analysis parameters affecting material strength, geometric variation, and blast load were incorporated into the RBDO, while design variables included geometric and material strength properties. For computational feasibility, a surrogate blast response model based on finite element results was developed for use in the RBDO. It was found that most cost-effective blast resistant designs tend to have a smaller number of girders of minimum depth with thick flanges and webs made of typical rather than high strength grades of steel and supporting a concrete slab of typical minimum thickness.

papers.title: Radiographic Fractal Dimension and Implant Stability: An Ex Vivo Study of Implant Design and Osteotomy Preparation
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Radiographic fractal dimension (FD) describes image-pattern complexity, but its relationship with immediate implant fixation remains uncertain. This study examined FD before osteotomy preparation and after implant placement in an ex vivo bovine-rib cohort. Materials and Methods: This secondary analysis included 80 blocks, with one implant per block, two implant designs, and four complete preparation protocols (n = 10 per combination). FD was calculated from periapical radiographs using 200 × 50-pixel ROIs. Factorial analyses, baseline-adjusted ANCOVA, and exploratory correlations were performed. Intraobserver reliability was assessed on 32 images measured twice. Results: Baseline FD differed among preparation-protocol groups (p = 0.025). Post-placement differences remained after baseline adjustment for design (p = 0.017) and protocol (p = 0.029), without a significant interaction (p = 0.587). No significant effects on ΔFD were detected for design (p = 0.251), protocol (p = 0.237), or interaction (p = 0.230). Weak nominal correlations of post-placement FD with insertion torque (r = 0.263) and ISQ (r = 0.222) did not retain significance after Holm correction; none of the correlations adjusted for experimental grouping was significant. The absolute-agreement, single-measurement ICC was 0.416 (95% CI, 0.077 to 0.667); matched reanalyses were approximately 0.108 FD units lower than the original values. Conclusions: Adjusted post-placement FD differences were not accompanied by significant between-group effects on ΔFD. Limited reliability, unresolved original-to-repeat disagreement and uncertain ROI correspondence constrain interpretation. These exploratory findings do not demonstrate procedure-induced structural changes or validate FD as a predictor of implant stability or osseointegration.

papers.title: Resolution-aware computational analysis of Korteweg-Helmholtz forcing in ternary ferro-nanofluid cooling using finite-element and physics-informed neural network models
papers.abstract: Reliable computational design of magnetically responsive coolants requires distinguishing physically resolvable transport effects from numerical artifacts. This study develops a resolution-aware computational framework for a shear-thinning Cu-Fe3O4-CoFe2O4 ternary ferro-nanofluid cooling a continuously stretching heated surface. The finite two-dimensional model employs the pressure-invariant Korteweg-Helmholtz force, $-\tfrac{1}{2}\mu _{0}H^{2}\nabla \chi _{\mathrm{eff}}$, driven by temperature-dependent susceptibility, together with species-specific Brownian, thermophoretic, and magnetophoretic transport. A monolithic Taylor-Hood finite-element solver recovers the Sakiadis and Crane limits and agrees with a high-Prandtl-number Robin asymptote. Systematic grid refinement gives a numerical uncertainty of 5.2 × 10−4 in the mean wall heat flux, which serves as the detectability threshold, while paired-difference uncertainties on the same meshes establish which parameter-induced differences are numerically resolved. A residence-time audit gives a particle-slip displacement of only 1.90 × 10−5 of the thermal-layer thickness, which justifies a uniform-composition reduction. Within the linear-magnetization regime, the magnetic response grows linearly with the magnetic number and reaches only 1.5 × 10−7 at a magnetic number of 20, far below this threshold, and remains below 0.3 of it at directly computed bounding conditions. Magnetic forcing is therefore locally present but not detectable in the global thermal response for magnets spanning the sheet. Increasing the surface heat transfer coefficient from 25 to 500 W m−2 K−1 raises the mean wall heat flux from 244 to 3287 W m−2, mainly through the imposed surface resistance. Composition produces a 0.103% span that is robustly resolved as a paired difference across the mesh sequence and is about twice the finest-grid uncertainty. However, it is below the 0.12% absolute uncertainty of the production mesh and is about eight times smaller than the 0.8% engineering-significance threshold associated with an assumed 1% uncertainty in the surface coefficient. Shear thinning mainly affects drag. A parameterized physics-informed neural network reproduces the fields of nine independent held-out parameter combinations with range-normalized errors of 0.025 to 0.14, but its errors of up to 23% and 50% in wall heat flux and Nusselt number restrict it to field-level screening, and its anchor and training cost is recovered only after about 103 evaluations. The framework provides quantitative criteria for separating detectable and engineering-significant responses from discretization-level signals.

papers.title: Precision Bone Regeneration: 3D/4D Bioprinting of Personalized Hydrogel Scaffolds with Regenerative Cells and Adaptive Properties
papers.abstract: Critical-size bone defects remain a formidable surgical challenge worldwide, exacting a significant toll on patients' quality of life and functional recovery every year. Conventional treatment strategies autografts, xenografts, and synthetic substitutes continue to face major clinical limitations, and despite decades of progress in biomaterials and tissue engineering, this challenge persists because traditional scaffolds are inherently static, unable to adapt to the dynamic, multi-phase biology of bone healing. This review explores how the convergence of 3D bioprinting precision, 4D stimuli-responsive adaptability, hydrogel biocompatibility, and regenerative cell integration is reshaping bone regeneration into an intelligent, responsive process. Drawing on current literature evaluated across biomaterials, hydrogel chemistry, regenerative cell sources, fabrication techniques, scaffold architecture, porosity, mechanical performance, biodegradation, and biological outcomes, the evidence consistently shows that integrating these four technologies yields outcomes far superior to any single approach alone. Mechanistically, 4D-responsive scaffolds mirror the evolving extracellular matrix during healing softening in the inflammatory phase to promote angiogenesis and stiffening during mineralization to support new bone formation while hydrogel matrices simultaneously enable nutrient diffusion and sustained paracrine factor delivery essential for regenerative success. Together, these findings position 3D/4D bioprinted hydrogel scaffolds as a genuine paradigm shift, moving bone tissue engineering from passive structural support toward intelligent, adaptive regenerative systems poised for clinical translation within the next 5–10 years, with the potential to redefine the standard of care for complex bone defect reconstruction.

papers.title: Antibacterial and radiopaque bone materials based on Cu,Na-doped β-tricalcium phosphate: phosphate cements and PMMA composites
papers.abstract: Bone cements allow complex bone defects to be filled precisely and with minimal invasiveness, which favors implant integration and stability. They can also be functionalized with bioactive or antibacterial agents to promote osseointegration and to prevent post-surgical infections. This study reports the synthesis, crystal structure and multifunctional properties of a new series of Cu, Na-co-doped β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) with the general formula Ca 10– x NaCu x (PO 4 ) 7 (NC x ); it has been developed both as antibacterial and bioactive phosphate bone cements and as radiopaque fillers for polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA)-based bone cements. The compounds were synthesized by high-temperature solid-state reaction and characterized by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) with Rietveld refinement and SEM, and their antibacterial activity and bioactive properties towards adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells (aMSCs) were evaluated. The behavior of aMSCs on the surface of the NC x phosphates investigated by the direct contact method was similar to the control. It was shown that the samples enhanced the osteogenic differentiation potential of aMSCs. Phosphate cements (NC x -cem) and PMMA–phosphate composites (PMMA–NC x ) were prepared from NC x powders. The antimicrobial efficacy against E. coli and S. aureus increased with Cu 2+ content: NC1.0 sample achieved complete inhibition of E. coli within 3 h, and the corresponding cements inhibited its growth effectively. The antibacterial activity of the PMMA–NC x composites was compared with those of commercial PMMA bone cement. The setting temperature of NC x -cem did not exceed 35 °C, and the addition of NCx powder to PMMA likewise lowered the hardening temperature to ≤35 °C. The mechanical properties of NC x -cem and PMMA–NC x composites were studied. NC x -cem exhibits high radiopacity, the X-ray attenuation increasing from 1500 HU for NC0.1-cem to 2300 HU for NC1.0-cem. Incorporated as a 15 wt% filler in PMMA bone cement, NC0.8 raised the attenuation of unfilled PMMA from 70 ± 10 HU to 610 ± 30 HU, which is sufficient for clear visualization by computed tomography (CT) imaging. These results show that Ca 10– x NaCu x (PO 4 ) 7 combines antibacterial activity, bioactive bone cement formation, and enhanced radiopacity in a single material, making it a promising multifunctional candidate for advanced bone tissue engineering and orthopedic applications.

papers.title: Complete Intrapelvic Migration of a Retained Kirschner Wire in a Failed Total Hip Arthroplasty: Fluoroscopy-Guided Open Retrieval After Failed Laparoscopic Localization
papers.abstract: Kirschner wires (K-wires) are occasionally used as improvised fixation for an intraoperative acetabular fracture (IAF) during uncemented total hip arthroplasty (THA). Unlike threaded screws, smooth wires provide no axial purchase, are prone to migration, and, when directed medially, may traverse the quadrilateral plate into the true pelvis. We report a 67-year-old woman who underwent staged bilateral uncemented THA elsewhere for bilateral osteonecrosis of the femoral head. The left-sided procedure was complicated by an intraoperative posterior wall acetabular fracture, fixed with multiple smooth K-wires beneath an attempted press-fit cup. Six weeks later, the acetabular component dislocated, and she was referred to our unit. Radiographs and computed tomography (CT) at presentation demonstrated a dislocated, vertically and laterally migrated cup; a deficient posterior wall; and five retained K-wires: two in the posterior wall, one backed out into the posterior soft tissues, and two lying almost entirely within the pelvis, differing only in the osseous purchase retained by their terminal segments. At revision, three wires were removed easily, and the intrapelvic wire that retained purchase was withdrawn intact along its original trajectory. The wire with minimal residual purchase lost its remaining anchorage during the extraction of the loose shell and migrated completely into the pelvis; blind retrieval was deliberately not attempted. The posterior wall was reconstructed with a structural femoral head allograft and a large porous-coated uncemented multi-hole cup (Continuum, Zimmer Biomet, Warsaw, IN). Postoperative imaging localized the wire in the left extraperitoneal paravesical tissue adjacent to the bladder. Diagnostic laparoscopy failed to identify it, and a left lower quadrant laparotomy was performed with intact retrieval. Transient mild hematuria settled with hydration alone, and recovery was otherwise uneventful. Smooth K-wires should be avoided as definitive fixation for periprosthetic acetabular fractures. When retained wires are predominantly intrapelvic at presentation, complete migration during the removal of a failed construct should be anticipated, disclosed at consent, and planned for with cross-sectional imaging and a pre-arranged multidisciplinary retrieval pathway.

papers.title: Timing of Total Hip Arthroplasty and Lumbar Spinal Fusion in Patients With Hip and Spine Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: Background Context Hip-spine syndrome involves concurrent hip and lumbar spine degeneration, often leading to overlapping symptoms that complicate management. The optimal surgical sequence between lumbar spine fusion (LSF) and total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains unclear. Purpose To evaluate the existing literature comparing surgical sequencing strategies and determine whether THA or LSF should be performed first in patients with hip-spine syndrome. Study Design/Setting Systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted per PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Methods PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched to gather studies directly comparing the surgical sequencing of THA and LSF in patients with hip-spine syndrome who have undergone both procedures. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Where appropriate, risk ratios were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and modified Hartung–Knapp confidence intervals. Results After screening 971 records, 19 studies were included. Five studies contributed to the principal dislocation synthesis, which showed no statistically significant association with surgical sequence (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.48–1.72; P = .692; I 2 = 11.6%). Replacing Welling with Bala shifted the estimate towards higher risk after LSF-first sequencing (RR 2.21, 95% CI 0.98–5.00), but the confidence interval included no association. Several large cohorts outside the principal synthesis reported higher dislocation risk following spine-first surgery. Evidence for infection, loosening, revision and functional outcomes was limited by differences in populations, definitions and follow-up. Conclusions The evidence does not establish a preferred surgical sequence for THA and LSF. The periprosthetic fracture association derives from a single administrative cohort (Bala et al) and may reflect differences in bone quality, osteoporosis, frailty, or coding inaccuracies. Unequal post-THA observation periods in this cohort also limit interpretation of the fracture findings and dislocation sensitivity analysis. Heterogeneous fusion constructs, inconsistently reported sacral or pelvic involvement, and residual confounding further limit certainty. Surgical sequencing should remain individualized pending higher-quality evidence.

papers.title: Surrogate-Based Prediction and Feasible Process-Window Identification for Fillet Welding Deformation Control in Adjustment Pipe–Flange Joints
papers.abstract: This study proposes a data-driven method to predict thermal deformation in adjustment Pipe–Flange fillet welds and identify welding process windows satisfying the allowable deformation criterion. Longitudinal shrinkage data at circumferential locations under different inner and outer heat-input conditions were obtained from Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW) root-pass experiments and finite element analysis (FEA). Kernel Density Estimation (KDE)–Ridge correction-based synthetic data generation supplemented the limited dataset and preserved its probability distribution and heat-input-related deformation trends. Synthetic data were combined with FEA data for various Pipe–Flange geometries to construct the training dataset. Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) and a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) predicted shrinkage deformation at eight circumferential locations. CatBoost trained on the combined FEA and synthetic dataset achieved mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.023–0.051 mm, 0.030–0.055 mm, and 0.812–0.942, respectively, outperforming MLP in accuracy and consistency, and was selected as the final surrogate model. Feasible InnerQ–OuterQ combinations satisfying the target deformation criterion were explored for given geometries, and the corresponding process windows were defined. Derived heat-input conditions were converted into welding-speed ranges expressed in centimeters per minute (CPM) using actual FCAW variables. The framework supplements limited data with synthetic samples, enabling deformation prediction and feasible process-window identification.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization of stellarator alpha-particle confinement using data-informed parameter spaces and dimensionality reduction
papers.abstract: Modern stellarators are typically designed by optimizing the shape of the plasma boundary surface, with the parameters taken to be Fourier amplitudes. Many promising optimization algorithms such as Bayesian methods require bound constraints on the parameters and are most efficient when each parameter is scaled similarly to the others. With the typical Fourier parameterization, it is unclear how to set these bounds: wide constraints lead to self-intersecting boundaries and frequent failures of the MHD equilibrium calculation, while tight bound constraints limit expressiveness. To address these issues, here we propose two new parameter spaces for stellarator optimization. Both begin with a dataset of existing stellarator boundaries. In the first approach, a quantile transformation is applied to each Fourier degree of freedom, mapping the data distribution to a uniform distribution on the unit interval. In the second approach, principal component analysis (PCA) is applied to points on the boundaries, followed by a quantile transformation. For both approaches, the transformed variables become the degrees of freedom, naturally bounded to [0, 1]. The PCA method has the additional benefit of dimensionality reduction, with high expressiveness for a small number of parameters. The methods are demonstrated via Bayesian optimization for good alpha-particle confinement with guiding-center tracing inside the optimization loop, using asynchronous parallelization. These optimizations yield stellarator configurations with excellent collisionless fast-particle confinement in fields that can be far from quasisymmetric or quasi-isodynamic.

papers.title: Parametric Probabilistic Manifold Decomposition for Nonlinear Model Reduction
papers.abstract: Probabilistic Manifold Decomposition (PMD) [ SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 48 (2026), pp. A209–A235], developed in our earlier work, provides a nonlinear model reduction by embedding high-dimensional dynamics onto low-dimensional probabilistic manifolds. The PMD has demonstrated strong performance for time-dependent systems. However, its formulation is for temporal dynamics and does not directly accommodate parametric variability, which limits its applicability to tasks such as design optimization, control, and uncertainty quantification. In order to address the limitations, a Parametric Probabilistic Manifold Decomposition (PPMD) method is presented to deal with parametric problems. The central advantage of PPMD is its ability to construct continuous, high-fidelity parametric surrogates while retaining the transparency and nonintrusive workflow of PMD. By integrating probabilistic-manifold embeddings with parameter-aware latent learning, PPMD enables smooth predictions across unseen parameter values (such as different boundary or initial conditions). To validate the proposed method, a comprehensive convergence analysis is established for PPMD, covering the approximation of the linear principal subspace, the geometric recovery of the nonlinear solution manifold, and the statistical consistency of the kernel ridge regression used for latent learning. The framework is then numerically demonstrated on two classic flow configurations: flow past a cylinder and backward-facing step flow. Results confirm that PPMD achieves superior accuracy and generalization beyond the training parameter range compared to the conventional proper orthogonal decomposition with Gaussian process regression (POD + GPR) method. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SISC and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://github.com/apprenticeGuo/Parametric-Probabilistic-Manifold-Decomposition-for-Nonlinear-Model-Reduction and in the supplementary materials ( Parametric-Probabilistic-Manifold-Decomposition-for-Nonlinear-Model-Reduction-main.zip [12.3KB]). papers.title: RMG-Py v4: 17 Years of Open-Source Reaction Mechanism Generation
papers.abstract: Kinetic modeling describes reacting chemical systems through networks of elementary reactions and their associated rate parameters. Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG-Py) automates the construction of these networks by simulating reaction fluxes to identify dominant chemical pathways in silico. RMG-Py v4.0.0 marks 17 years of open-source reaction mechanism generation, introducing substantial improvements in performance, usability, and chemical scope. Benchmarks demonstrate higher throughput in constructing combustion models relative to prior versions, alongside streamlined installation via Docker and binary distributions. Key new capabilities include automated library selection, improved species selection algorithms, integration with the Julia-based ReactionMechanismSimulator.jl for simulating arbitrary reactor configurations, and PySIDT-based property estimators. Heterogeneous catalysis support is improved by the addition of new adsorbate thermophysical property data, new reaction families, resonance templates of surface-bound species, and uncertainty quantification for parameter sensitivity analysis. The release also extends RMG-Py into new chemical domains, including electrochemical mechanisms for battery and CO2RR applications, and an automated fragment-based modeling framework for the pyrolysis of large molecules. Together, these advances improve new users’ experience, expand the range of tractable systems, and maintain RMG-Py at the forefront of computational kinetic modeling.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification in data-driven dynamical models via inverse problem solving
papers.abstract: Data-driven model identification strategies can be used to obtain phenomenological models that capture the temporal evolution of observable data. While it is usually straightforward to obtain such a model from time series data, for instance with least-squares fitting, it is generally difficult to quantify the uncertainty associated with the prediction of the temporal evolution of the observables. This paper considers a general framework for uncertainty quantification in data-driven dynamical models by framing prediction error through the lens of inverse problem theory. Building on Koopman-inspired model identification strategies that are suited for nonlinear dynamical models, we consider a prediction as an approximate measurement from which the original input state can be faithfully recovered, and define the prediction error as the MSE of solving the inverse problem that would yield this prediction. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach on both numerical models and experimental data showing that it provides a robust uncertainty measure of model performance.

papers.title: A hybrid framework for uncertainty quantification in partially observed dynamic biological systems
papers.abstract: Mechanistic ordinary differential equation (ODE) models are widely used in systems biology, but uncertainty quantification (UQ) remains difficult when only a subset of state variables is experimentally observed. Existing Bayesian and likelihood-based approaches can be computationally demanding for nonlinear, weakly identifiable, or high-dimensional systems. We present a framework, and its corresponding software CUQDyn1_Plus , for UQ in partially observed ODE systems. Our method combines leave-one-out jackknife+-style empirical calibration for observed states with sensitivity-based Gaussian uncertainty propagation for hidden states. The software supports global parameter estimation, covariance propagation, bootstrap trajectory uncertainty and simulation-based calibration. It also facilitates comparison with Bayesian workflows, automated reporting, and reproducibility diagnostics. Validation on six benchmark systems shows accurate behavior in well-conditioned cases and model-dependent degradation under nonlinearity, weak identifiability, or global branch-switching non-identifiability. CUQDyn1_Plus provides a practical and computationally efficient UQ workflow for systems biology models with observed and latent states. Its diagnostic outputs help identify when local Gaussian propagation is reliable and when uncertainty bands should be interpreted cautiously, making it a useful complement to fully Bayesian workflows.

papers.title: Geometry-based prediction of built imperfections for additively manufactured complex metamaterials
papers.abstract: Despite the high structural flexibility offered by additive manufacturing (AM), the effective manufacturability of complex metamaterials with highly non-periodic architectures is often limited by process-induced defects such as unsupported overhangs, disconnected features, and enclosed cavities. These limitations are particularly critical for disordered structures, where geometric complexity precludes straightforward design rules and systematic screening. We present an algorithmic framework that relies solely on geometric criteria to detect critical features in laser-based powder bed fusion printing. The method, based on persistent homology and local geometric criteria, identifies regions prone to fabrication failure through voxel-based analysis, including unsupported material, restricted-access voids, and weak connections. These criteria are combined into a unified procedure to assess the printability of candidate structures prior to manufacturing. The approach is demonstrated on spinodoid metamaterials, whose morphologies provide an ideal test case for complex and/or disordered structures. To experimentally validate the proposed methodology, comparisons with several samples produced by laser-based powder bed fusion of metals using 316L stainless steel powder are presented. Overall, we see that all critical defects were correctly isolated from other structural arrangements. The presented framework, which can be extended to other structures and AM techniques, enables efficient, process-aware screening of complex architectures and can be applied to complement the design of other metamaterials incorporating manufacturability.

papers.title: An AI-based framework for assessing physical fitness, energy metabolism, and biomechanical efficiency in sprinting and hurdle events
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of physiological and biomechanical parameters is essential for intelligent sports analytics, personalized training, and health monitoring. However, existing approaches rarely model temporal, cross-signal, and physical relationships within a single framework. This study proposes a hybrid Transformer–GNN–PINN framework for the continuous multi-output regression of multimodal physiological and biomechanical variables. The framework was evaluated on a synthetic multimodal dataset comprising 100 simulated participant profiles and 50,000 samples (0.1 s each) representing sprinting and hurdling across four performance levels; no human participants were involved. The inputs comprise heart rate, oxygen saturation, triaxial acceleration, triaxial angular velocity, and acceleration magnitude, and the targets are velocity, oxygen consumption (VO 2 ), energy expenditure, heart rate, and biomechanical efficiency. Simulated values were bounded by physiological ranges reported in the exercise-physiology and sprint-biomechanics literature. The model combines Transformer and Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) blocks for attention-based feature encoding and variable selection, a graph neural network (GNN) over a fixed sensor-channel graph, and physics-informed loss terms for motion and energy consistency. On a participant-level held-out test set, the model achieved a macro-averaged MAE of 0.085, RMSE of 0.140, and R 2 of 0.93 in standardized units. These results indicate the potential of combining attention-based, graph-based, and physics-based learning for multimodal sports prediction under simulated conditions; validation with real athlete data is required before practical use.

papers.title: Indiscriminate poisoning attacks on malware concept drift adaptation via sample selection decision stealing for inducing fabricated concept drift
papers.abstract: Machine learning dominates modern malware detection but suffers persistent performance degradation from concept drift. Active learning-based concept drift adaptation (CDA-AL) mitigates this problem by selecting informative samples for retraining, yet its security vulnerabilities remain underexplored. We show that adversaries can exploit CDA-AL’s sample-selection mechanism by injecting clean-label poisoned samples with attacker-induced high uncertainty. These poisoned samples are optimized to exhibit high uncertainty under the victim’s active-selection criterion, although their apparent informativeness is unrelated to the genuine cross-cycle distribution shift. By competing with genuine drift samples for the limited labeling budget, they reduce the opportunities for genuine drift samples to enter the retraining set and thereby suppress adaptation to the evolving data distribution. We present STEAL, a clean-label poisoning attack against CDA-AL-based malware detectors. STEAL uses knowledge distillation to train a surrogate that approximates the victim’s sample-selection preference, applies uncertainty-greedy feature perturbation to generate high-priority poisoned samples, and injects them into the unlabeled pool. Experiments on two large-scale real-world malware datasets show that STEAL degrades performance across seven CDA-AL strategies at 96.5% of evaluated time points and outperforms six attack baselines. It reduces F1 by 41.43% on APIGraph and 42.44% on AndroZoo, corresponding to 8 \(\times\) and 6.5 \(\times\) the degradation of the strongest baseline while increasing false negative rates to 60.40% and 68.76%, respectively. Finally, we propose a lightweight defense using geometric outlierness and structural rarity, improving F1 scores by 66.98% and 91.54% on APIGraph and AndroZoo, respectively.
