papers.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-assisted problem-based learning in undergraduate emergency medicine education: a self-controlled study
papers.abstract: Background Emergency medicine education requires strong clinical reasoning, rapid decision-making, and effective teamwork. Although problem-based learning (PBL) has been widely adopted in medical education, its implementation is often constrained by the need for substantial faculty resources, standardized case development, and continuous support for self-directed learning. With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI), ChatGPT has emerged as a promising educational tool. This study aimed to evaluate the educational outcomes associated with a ChatGPT-assisted PBL teaching model in undergraduate emergency medicine education. Methods A self-controlled before-and-after study was conducted in 2024 among 121 fourth-year medical students from the Class of 2021. Students first completed a traditional teaching phase followed by a ChatGPT-assisted PBL phase. Student satisfaction was assessed after each instructional phase using an anonymous questionnaire. At the end of the course, students completed a comprehensive final examination, and scores for chapters taught using the two instructional approaches were analyzed separately. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 29.0. Results Compared with the traditional teaching phase, the ChatGPT-assisted PBL phase demonstrated significantly higher student satisfaction regarding the teaching model, theoretical knowledge acquisitio n , perceived clinical reasoning development, and perceived teamwork improvement (all P < 0.05). Students also achieved significantly higher examination scores (mean difference, 8.74 points; 95% CI, 7.16–10.31; P < 0.001) and higher pass rates ( P < 0.001). Qualitative feedback suggested that students perceived the AI-assisted model as promoting classroom interaction, active learning, and collaborative problem-solving. Conclusions The combined ChatGPT-assisted PBL model was associated with higher student satisfaction and better theoretical examination performance than the preceding traditional teaching phase in undergraduate emergency medicine education. Because both the instructional approach and the use of ChatGPT were introduced simultaneously, the independent contribution of ChatGPT cannot be determined. Further studies using more rigorous study designs are needed to evaluate the educational impact of AI-assisted PBL.

papers.title: Robust control of active suspension systems via a physics-informed neural network and adaptive backstepping terminal sliding mode control
papers.abstract: In this paper, a control framework is developed for a 2-degree-of-freedom quarter-car active suspension with unknown sprung-channel drift and input gain. The unknown maps are reconstructed by a decoupled physics-informed neural network. Two sub-networks estimate the drift and the gain separately, and the governing equation of the actuated channel enters the training loss as a residual on an unlabelled collocation set, positivity of the gain is imposed by the output architecture instead of by a penalty, and a three-stage schedule spends the excitation along the input direction on the gain. The estimates drive an adaptive backstepping non-singular terminal sliding-mode law with a continuous reaching law and projected, σ -modified adaptation. Because the plant is underactuated, cancelling the drift in full makes the command reproduce the suspension force and leaves the wheel-hop mode undamped. A retention coefficient returns a fraction of that force to the wheel, and the certificate is uniform in it. A composite Lyapunov argument establishes uniform ultimate boundedness of the tracking error, the sliding variable and the weights, boundedness of the unactuated channel, and sufficient conditions on the rattle space and tyre load. On an ISO 8608 class C road, the estimator attains a mean multiplicative gain error of 3.43% against 11.48% for a radial-basis approximator on the same data. The closed loop lowers the ISO 2631-1 weighted acceleration by 26.0% against a passive suspension and by 11.1% against the same law driven by that approximator, at a dynamic tyre load ratio of 0.85 and inside the actuator limit.

papers.title: Risk-aware adaptive hierarchical diffusion for communication fault diagnosis and joint communication-edge computing resource scheduling in cyber-physical power systems
papers.abstract: Dynamic power communication networks must jointly allocate routes, transmission bandwidth, edge-computing cycles, traffic admission, and service priorities while preserving the latency and reliability requirements of protection and control services. Existing deterministic optimizers and single-pass reinforcement-learning policies have difficulty representing multiple high-quality allocations and maintaining instantaneous feasibility when traffic, topology, and electrical operating conditions change simultaneously. This paper proposes a risk-aware adaptive hierarchical diffusion policy for joint communication and computing resource scheduling. The scheduling problem is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process over a four-level architecture comprising core routing, edge computation, access bandwidth, and service control. A coarse-to-fine conditional reverse process generates the four action groups sequentially, while service-risk and constraint gradients guide each intermediate sample. A state-complexity controller adjusts the denoising depth online, and a risk-weighted projection maps the terminal sample to the state-dependent feasible set. The method is evaluated on an 18-node communication network coupled with a modified IEEE 33-bus distribution system under four traffic classes and disturbance-driven workloads. Across 30 random seeds, the proposed policy achieves the lowest weighted delay and deadline-violation ratio among priority queuing, constrained model predictive control, proximal policy optimization, soft actor-critic, and fixed-step diffusion baselines, while preserving admitted throughput and fairness. Ablation and depth-sensitivity results further show that hierarchical conditioning, trajectory-level safety guidance, and adaptive reverse depth serve complementary roles. These results support diffusion-based scheduling as a feasible approach to risk-sensitive resource coordination in dynamic power communication networks.

A quantitative, descriptive-correlational design using structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed. Through total enumeration, 278 BTLEd students of the Main Campus and Biliran Campus of Biliran Province State University, Philippines, answered a survey composed of adopted measures of ICT use, technology-enabled active learning, course engagement, and DigComp-based digital competence, with pilot-test reliability coefficients ranging from 0.651 to 0.865. Data were analyzed using frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation, SEM, and mediation analysis. The respondents were mostly 21–25 years old, female, fourth-year, and Home Economics students; 94.24% relied mainly on smartphones, and 54.32% had no formal ICT training. All four constructs were rated Strongly Agree, with the lowest item ratings in voluntarily contributing ideas in class, using advanced videoconferencing features, and organizing and analyzing data. papers.title: Ioxhēn ∿ Vq–EVE - Exact Tail-Profile Compilation with Preserved Covariance, Minimum-Movement Scenario Control, and Sharp Total-Variation Mixing
papers.abstract: How much can tail risk change while the mean, full covariance matrix, and directional kurtosis stay fixed? The central result gives necessary and sufficient conditions for prescribing both the counts in separated bins of a squared standardized projection and the fourth moment in that direction. It computes the full feasible kurtosis interval and constructs any feasible target with one scalar quadratic solve. A rank-two covariance completion then realizes the selected signed projection values with minimum squared movement for the fixed labels in whitened coordinates. The work also gives a controller for changing kurtosis after compilation. With \(m\) antithetic pairs, it reaches any compatible target in at most \(m-1\) two-column rotations, each affecting four scenarios. Every intermediate step preserves the mean, full covariance, equal weights, and each scenario’s assigned bin. The controller can pause after any rotation and resume from the resulting ensemble. For a selected pair and a specified movement budget, the manuscript derives the exact reachable range of a single fourth moment and gives a quartic solver for a weighted objective across multiple directional fourth moments. Gaussian smoothing yields a strictly positive density with the prescribed population covariance. For a nonlinear averaging process with fixed smoothed forcing and reset probability \(\varepsilon\), matching upper and worst-case lower bounds give the sharp uniform total-variation rate \((1-\varepsilon)^t\) over centered distributions with identity covariance. For \(\varepsilon>1/2\), a direct branching-tree sampler draws from the stationary law without burn-in. At \(\varepsilon=0.75\), it uses 1.5 terminal scenario draws on average, followed by one Gaussian vector. The release includes 768 synthetic five-channel scenarios across three profiles. papers.abstract: In structural reliability analysis, surrogate models are essential for efficiently simulating complex mechanical systems, significantly reducing the computational demands of time‐intensive simulations. Traditional sampling methods often overlook the spatial importance of input data, including unnecessary data points that do not enhance prediction accuracy or computational efficiency. This study introduces a novel active learning strategy employing an adaptive proximity‐based weighted interpolation (PBWI) technique, effectively coupled with multi‐response Gaussian process regression (MRGPR) models. By prioritizing samples that minimize uncertainty in these critical zones for inclusion in the surrogate models, the proposed methodology significantly improves model fidelity and reduces the number of performance function evaluations. Rigorous validations across diverse numerical and structural scenarios, including series and complex parallel systems, confirm these enhancements. This approach distinctly contrasts with traditional surrogate‐based probability of failure evaluation methods and highlights the innovative potential of this advanced active learning framework.

papers.abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has been widely investigated for quadrotor trajectory tracking because it optimizes control inputs while explicitly handling constraints. To address this limitation, Gaussian processes (GPs) have been used to estimate unknown disturbances and incorporate them into the MPC prediction model. Conventional GP-based methods directly represent disturbances as stochastic processes without explicitly encoding system dynamics in the GP model and may therefore require substantial training data for accurate estimation. This study proposes an MPC-based trajectory tracking method with online disturbance estimation using a multi-output physics-informed Gaussian process (PI-GP). The PI-GP embeds physical relationships among position, velocity, and disturbances derived from a simplified linear translational model into its covariance structure while accounting for correlations among the three axes. The resulting disturbance estimates are incorporated into MPC state predictions. The proposed method is evaluated against conventional GP-based MPC through numerical simulations in terms of disturbance estimation accuracy and trajectory tracking performance. The simulations show lower position tracking errors and improved disturbance estimation in most tested conditions, particularly with short regression windows.

Neuroscience has described with increasing precision how curiosity, reward prediction error and retrieval modulate memory formation, yet this knowledge rarely reaches lesson design in a usable form. Aim. To build and document a theory-driven 3D model that shows how one teaching message travels through the learning brain under two teaching styles, to report what classroom deployments of the resulting design suggest, and to derive practical design principles for Gen Z, ADHD and dyslexic learners. Methods. Multi-method design combining (1) a structured narrative review of 59 sources, weighted towards experimental, meta-analytic and 2025 to 2026 evidence; (2) construction of an interactive 3D teaching model on a real cortical surface (FreeSurfer fsaverage5, 20,484 vertices) with 28 nodes at approximate MNI coordinates, eight functional systems and two scripted message routes, the classic lecture (five steps) and the dopamine loop (six steps), each step traced to published findings; (3) descriptive analysis of anonymised platform data from the two loop-structured workshops with complete platform exports (n = 141 and n = 22), held in Prague in November 2026 as part of a wider series of guest sessions at universities, study-abroad programmes and a secondary school; and (4) design synthesis. The model renders a lecture route in which a dense message overloads working memory (about four chunks), generates little reward prediction error and hands attention to the default mode network, and a loop route in which a curiosity gap recruits the salience network, midbrain dopamine and hippocampus, a prediction-then-reveal step produces a learning signal, and retrieval, peer feedback and a focus sprint strengthen the memory trace. In the two documented pilots, 91% and 81% of quiz items were answered correctly at the first attempt, and 40% and 77% of students completed all seven chapters; neither pilot had a control group or a delayed retention test. Conclusions. The dopamine loop is best understood not as a way to give students pleasure but as a way to create, resolve and store prediction errors at a rhythm that fits human working memory. The monograph proposes a six-move lesson cycle (curiosity gap, prediction, reveal, retrieval, social feedback, focus sprint), specific adaptations for ADHD and dyslexia, and guardrails for AI tutors, together with testable hypotheses for a controlled trial. papers.title: Factors Affecting the Mechanical Properties of Biomimetic Schwarz Primitive TPMS Structures Printed from Glass-Filled Polyamide: A Multivariate Regression Analysis
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures have attracted considerable attention as lightweight architected materials for energy absorption and load-bearing applications. However, the combined influence of relative density and surface curvature on the mechanical behavior of glass-filled polyamide TPMS structures fabricated by selective laser sintering (SLS) remains insufficiently understood. In this study, biomimetic Schwarz Primitive TPMS structures with different values of the geometric parameter t were manufactured by SLS and experimentally investigated under quasi-static compression. The relationships between surface geometry, relative density, deformation behavior, mechanical properties, and energy absorption were analyzed. The results demonstrate that, in addition to relative density, the absolute value of the average signed curvature is associated with changes in the elastic modulus, compressive strength, deformation mode, and energy absorption capability of the structures. A structural approach for evaluating the effective plasticity of cellular materials based on their deformation behavior is proposed. Specimens with t values close to zero exhibited stable progressive collapse characterized by an extended stress plateau, whereas the maximum volumetric energy absorption (1.814 MJ/m3) was obtained for the structure with t = 0.3. In contrast, the structure with t = 0.9 exhibited premature failure at a limiting strain of 12.5% without reaching the densification stage. Comparison of experimental measurements with numerical homogenization revealed a systematic underestimation of Young’s modulus by the numerical model. Following calibration against the experimental reference configuration, a multivariate regression analysis was performed to quantify the relative contributions of relative density and absolute value of the average signed curvature to the effective Young’s modulus of SLS-printed glass-filled polyamide TPMS structures. The standardized regression coefficients indicated that, for the investigated SLS-printed glass-filled polyamide TPMS structures, the association between the absolute value of the average signed curvature and Young’s modulus was approximately 3.65 times stronger than that between relative density and Young’s modulus within the investigated dataset. Additional numerical homogenization analysis of the Gyroid topology was performed to examine the consistency of this relationship across different TPMS architectures. The results obtained provide practical guidelines for optimizing TPMS architectures with respect to strength, weight, and specific energy absorption, highlighting their potential for lightweight engineering and protective applications.

papers.title: Efficacy of BOPPPS-based learning versus lecture-based learning in medical education: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background The BOPPPS instructional model (bridge-in, objective, pretest, participatory learning, posttest, summary) is a modular, student-centered framework designed to enhance engagement and active learning. Lecture-based learning (LBL) remains the most widely used traditional teaching approach in medical education. This meta-analysis compared the effects of BOPPPS-based instruction versus LBL on multiple learning outcomes in medical education. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to October 10, 2026, for randomized and non-randomized controlled trials comparing pure BOPPPS interventions with LBL. Meta-analyses were conducted using Review Manager 5.4 and Stata 17.0. Results Thirteen studies were included. Compared with LBL, BOPPPS yielded statistically significant improvements across all outcomes: comprehensive scores (SMD=0.65, 95% CI: 0.22–1.08, P = 0.003), theoretical knowledge (SMD=0.73, 95% CI: 0.52–0.94, P < 0.001), application competencies (SMD=1.63, 95% CI: 0.96–2.31, P < 0.001), learning motivation (SMD=0.77, 95% CI: 0.49–1.05, P < 0.001), critical thinking (SMD=0.99, 95% CI: 0.38–1.60, P = 0.001), case analysis (SMD=0.71, 95% CI: 0.41–1.02, P < 0.001) and students’ satisfaction (SMD=1.05, 95% CI: 0.72–1.38, P < 0.001). Conclusion BOPPPS-based instruction was associated with improved learning outcomes across most domains compared with LBL in medical education. Given the substantial heterogeneity, mixed evidence of publication bias, and limited geographic diversity of the included studies, these findings should be regarded as supportive rather than conclusive. High-quality, multicenter studies are needed to confirm these results. Systematic Review Registration PROSPERO (CRD42025630581).

papers.title: Integration of Nanotechnology and 3D Printing for Next-Generation Drug Delivery Systems
papers.abstract: Incorporating nanotechnology and three-dimensional (3D) printing have recently emerged as a strategy for creating next-generation drug delivery systems that offer a better level of control of drug loading, release, spatial distribution, and dosage-form design. Nanotechnology offers the advantage of nanoscale platforms such as nanoparticles, liposomes, nanogels, nanocrystals and nanocomposites that can assist in improving the protection and controlled delivery of drugs and 3D printing provides the advantage of customised structures that have controlled geometry and internal architecture. The combination of their two components allows for multiscale control, linking nanoscale properties of drug carrier functions with digitally designed 3D structures. This review covers the basics of nanotechnology and pharmaceutical 3D printing, integration strategies, fabrication methods, drug loading/release mechanisms, and drug delivery applications such as oral, localized, implantable, transdermal, tissue related, and personalized drug delivery. Recent developments, major advantages and challenges are also discussed. There are several challenges, such as material compatibility, dispersion and printability of nanoparticles, drug stability, reproducibility, scale-up, biological safety, quality control, and regulatory demands. Key to successful translation will be optimized materials, manufacturing processes, standardized characterization, and quality assurance in order to overcome these challenges. Overall, a flexible platform for the controlled, personalized and multifunctional drug delivery system is provided by nano-enabled 3D printing.

papers.abstract: This paper investigates an active interference strategy for gliding vehicles subject to uncertain dynamic constraints, with modeling based on optimal control. A gliding vehicle executes evasive maneuvers to actively interfere with the radar systems’ trajectory estimation and prediction, which employs the Singer model combined with an extended Kalman filter (EKF). Distinct from existing studies that primarily adopt threat-zone circumvention strategies, this paper proposes an incremental model predictive control (IMPC)-based maneuver method for gliding vehicle, enabling quantitative analysis of the radar systems’ trajectory estimation and prediction process with the objective of generating sufficiently large prediction errors. First, based on the time-scale separation (TSS) principle, the nonlinear flight dynamics are transformed into a weakly model-dependent incremental linear dynamic system. Second, the error bounds of the incremental linearization are established, and the system is discretized. On this basis, under multiple uncertain dynamic constraints, the IMPC-based maneuver method is developed to maximize the radar system’s prediction errors during the detection and tracking phase. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to examine the effectiveness and computational cost of the proposed strategy.

papers.title: Digital twin of brain neural systems: Opportunities for computational mechanics and AI
papers.abstract: Brain neural systems combine tissue mechanics, interstitial and cerebrospinal-fluid coupling, growth and remodeling, and electrically active neuronal networks across scales from synapses to whole-brain function. Modeling these systems to obtain clinically relevant predictions is the main promise of brain digital twins: subject-specific computational models updated through an observation–prediction–decision–observation loop. This work examines the emerging convergence of computational mechanics and artificial intelligence (AI) for such twins, using biomechanics as the organizing lens. We define a brain neural system digital twin as a closed loop that links separate modules. These may include imaging, electrophysiology, mechanistic models, parameter inference, uncertainty estimation, and decision support. Five complementary roles for AI are highlighted: image-to-model pipelines, inverse problems and personalization, surrogate and reduced-order modeling, data assimilation, and uncertainty quantification. We illustrate this framework across seven application domains and outline a verification, validation, and credibility framework needed for translation. We conclude that brain neural system twins can benefit from the integration of AI and numerical simulations into physics-grounded and uncertainty-based predictive workflows.

papers.title: Rapid indirect tyre pressure monitoring using adaptive forgetting extended kalman filter
papers.abstract: Tyre pressure monitoring constitutes a fundamental feature that influences the safety and economy performances of vehicles. However, the existing tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS) exhibits poor update frequency and expensive maintenance costs. To address these issues and identify the tyre blowout instant promptly, this paper proposes a rapid indirect tyre pressure estimation algorithm using an adaptive forgetting extended Kalman filter (AFEKF). The stiffness of four tyres is defined as state variables to formulate a nonlinear state-space of full-vehicle suspension dynamics. Further, the framework of AFEKF is developed. It integrates a forgetting factor to prioritize the latest data and employs innovation-based adaptive adjustment for measurement noise covariance matrix to compensate for modeling errors. In addition, using the normalized innovation square (NIS) of the sprung and unsprung mass accelerations, the instant of tyre blowout can be detected timely. Finally, the validations and comparisons under multiple scenarios are conducted on CarSim-Matlab/Simulink co-simulation platform. The results indicate that the AFEKF demonstrates more satisfactory estimation performance both in accuracy and stability than extended Kalman filter (EKF) and forgetting extended Kalman filter (FEKF). Moreover, it enables rapid identification of tyre blowout events within 5 ms by NIS. These verify the effectiveness and superiority of AFEKF for rapid tyre pressure monitoring.

papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of the martensite start temperature ( M s ) is critical for the design and industrial processing of advanced steels. This article provides a comprehensive state‐of‐the‐art review of M s prediction methods spanning eight decades (1940–2025), organized into four methodological eras: empirical linear regression, thermodynamic CALPHAD‐based models, pure machine learning approaches, and hybrid physics‐informed ML. All methods are evaluated within a four‐dimensional framework encompassing accuracy, accessibility, uncertainty quantification (UQ), and sustainability. Hybrid ML–physics models achieve root‐mean‐square errors (RMSE) of 12.15–14 K with R 2 up to 0.95 on novel compositions, representing a substantial improvement over earlier empirical equations while reducing CO 2 emissions by four to five orders of magnitude relative to full CALPHAD workflows. Standardized UQ evaluation protocols and a practitioner decision framework mapping use‐case scenarios to recommended methods are proposed. Emerging roles of large language models and generative AI (GenAI) in M s research, open reproducibility challenges, and ethical governance considerations are also addressed.

papers.abstract: Artificial hair implantation, also termed synthetic or biofiber hair implantation, is a percutaneous prosthetic procedure in which individual synthetic fibers are anchored in the scalp to provide immediate cosmetic density. Although the technique may appeal to patients with androgenetic alopecia, cicatricial alopecia, scalp scars, or limited donor hair, its safety remains controversial. This narrative review summarizes the historical, regulatory, clinical, and histopathologic evidence on artificial hair implantation and examines contemporary materials, patient selection, procedural principles, outcomes, and complication management. Early-generation implants were associated with rapid fiber loss, recurrent infection, foreign-body granulomas, scarring alopecia, and persistent inflammation, leading to the prohibition of prosthetic hair fibers in the United States under 21 CFR 895.101. Contemporary polyamide-based systems have renewed interest in selected regions, but the supporting evidence consists mainly of uncontrolled observational studies and case reports with inconsistent follow-up and adverse-event reporting. Immediate visual coverage is the most consistently reported benefit. Important risks include folliculitis, chronic suppuration, granulomatous inflammation, extrusion or breakage, scarring, and the eventual need for complete or staged fiber removal. The central biological limitation is the long-term maintenance of a low-inflammatory percutaneous interface exposed to friction, micromotion, sebum, and microbial colonization. Where legally permitted, the procedure should be considered a maintenance-dependent prosthetic option rather than a biological treatment. Careful selection, explicit informed consent, structured surveillance, prompt infection control, and early consideration of removal for refractory complications are essential. Long-term registries and standardized outcome reporting are needed.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN PHARMACEUTICAL FORMULATION DEVELOPMENT: FROM TRIAL-AND-ERROR TO PREDICTIVE AND AUTONOMOUS FORMULATION DESIGN
papers.abstract: Pharmaceutical formulation development has long relied on sequential experimentation in which formulation scientists select active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), excipients, compositions, and process parameters, manufacture prototypes, characterize critical quality attributes (CQAs), and iteratively modify unsuccessful formulations. While this approach remains valuable, it can become less efficient when formulation spaces expand and relationships among material attributes, process parameters, and product performance become nonlinear. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning, Bayesian optimization, natural language processing, and related computational approaches are enabling a transition toward predictive formulation development. These methods can bring together formulation composition, API descriptors, excipient characteristics, process variables, and analytical outcomes to predict CQAs such as dissolution, particle size, viscosity, stability, drug release, encapsulation efficiency, and manufacturability. Recent work has demonstrated ML-assisted excipient selection, prediction of tablet drug-release profiles, AI-assisted liquid formulation development, and Bayesian optimization for formulation experimentation. A promising next step is inverse formulation design, in which the desired product profile is specified first and algorithms identify candidate compositions and process conditions that are most likely to achieve it. Integration with Quality by Design (QbD), Design of Experiments (DoE), Process Analytical Technology (PAT), automated experimentation, digital twins, and robotics could ultimately create closed-loop or autonomous formulation laboratories. However, model reliability is limited by small and biased datasets, inconsistent experimental metadata, lack of external validation, explainability challenges, domain shift, data leakage, and uncertainty concerning regulatory qualification. This review discusses the evolution from empirical formulation development to predictive and autonomous workflows, major AI methods, applications across dosage forms, implementation with QbD and manufacturing, validation and regulatory considerations, research gaps, and future perspectives. The central argument of this review is that AI should support—not replace—formulation science and scientific judgement by reducing unnecessary experiments, prioritizing informative experiments, and accelerating translation of formulation knowledge into robust drug products.

papers.title: Formation Recovery and Velocity-Level Disturbance Rejection for Differential-Drive Mobile Robots
papers.abstract: This study quantifies the contributions of velocity regulation and formation-distance correction in a torque-actuated leader–follower cascade for three differential-drive robots subject to slip, skid, model mismatch, and matched disturbances. The cascade combines linear time-varying model predictive control (LTV–MPC), projected distance correction, and a torque-level inner loop. Proportional–integral (PI), conventional sliding-mode control (SMC), and PI-type dynamic sliding-mode control (DSMC) are calibrated within 0.5% of a common torque-variation target on a separate five-run set, then evaluated in 30 paired Monte Carlo trials per configuration, scenario, and path. Under persistent matched bias on the rounded-square path, PI-type DSMC reduces linear- and angular-velocity RMSE relative to SMC by 22.6% and 41.5%, while increasing path-tracking and formation RMSE by 5.0% and 9.7%. All tested sliding variables remain inside their boundary layers, where the unsaturated PI-type DSMC law is algebraically equivalent to PI control. With this inner loop, formation correction reduces conditional mean recovery time on the rounded-square path from 3.03 to 2.03 s after follower disturbances and from 4.06 to 2.48 s after leader disturbances. The recovered event fractions increase from 95.2% and 85.7% to 100%. A factorial comparison shows recovery benefits with all three inner loops, exceeding the spread between corrected inner loops. These benefits involve path-dependent tracking costs: event-window follower path RMSE increases by up to 7.5% on the rounded-square path. On both rose paths, the corrected and uncorrected PI-type DSMC configurations eventually recover but violate clearance in every follower-disturbance observation window. These violations are geometric footprint overlaps in a model without contact dynamics. The results distinguish velocity regulation, formation recovery, and clearance, and expose the limits of bounded correction under constrained velocity commands.

papers.title: Deep Learning and Intelligent Monitoring in Extrusion-Based Bioprinting: A Systematic Review - Suplementary data
papers.abstract: Extrusion-based bioprinting (EBB) is increasingly combined with deep learning (DL) to monitor, predict, and control the printing process, yet the degree of DL–hardware coupling achieved remains poorly characterized. This systematic review analysed 22 studies (2022–2026) applying DL to EBB, extracting methodological, technical, and reproducibility-related data, complemented by a TRIPOD+AI/PROBAST-based quality assessment. Convolutional architectures predominate in the vision pipeline, primarily for offline classification of print quality from imaging data, while regression models predict printing parameters, filament properties, and cell viability. Input data are largely restricted to process-monitoring images and printing parameters, with rheological information rarely exploited despite being available. Optical imaging is the dominant sensing modality, and multimodal sensor fusion remains rare. Most systems operate without feedback control or in open-loop configurations, with closed-loop, hardware-integrated control in a single case. External validation, uncertainty reporting, and statistical significance testing are infrequent, and source code and dataset availability remain limited despite growing adoption of open-science practices in research. Collectively, these findings indicate that DL applications in EBB remain predominantly confined to offline prediction and decision-support roles, with a pronounced maturity gap toward autonomous, closed-loop intelligent control. The review underscores the need for standardized reporting, multimodal integration, and benchmark datasets.

papers.abstract: Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) bone cement remains a mainstay of bone reconstruction, yet its high polymerization exotherm, mismatched stiffness, bioinertness and lack of antibacterial activity can lead to thermal injury, stress shielding and post-operative infection. Here we report a single-phase strategy that addresses these limitations together. Mesoporous calcium-silicate nanoparticles (MCSNs) and silver-templated MCSNs (Ag-MCSNs) were dispersed in a thermosensitive chitosan-glycerophosphate (CS-GP) hydrogel and blended with PMMA to prepare three modified cements. The hydrogel phase lowered the peak polymerization temperature from ∼77 °C to below 40 °C, extended the working time beyond 20 min and created interconnected pores throughout the PMMA matrix with a dominant pore diameter of ∼79 µm. The modified cements exhibited an elastic modulus of 140-170 MPa and a compressive yield strength of 7-10 MPa, closely matching cancellous bone, and these properties were retained after 28 days of immersion in simulated body fluid. The MCSN-containing cements additionally promoted apatite deposition, with cumulative calcium uptake reaching 2.8-3.3 mmol L-1 at day 28. Antibacterial testing against E. coli and S. aureus showed that only the Ag-MCSN cement produced clear inhibition zones, disrupted bacterial membranes on contact, and significantly reduced the number of recoverable colonies (p < 0.05) without compromising cytocompatibility. A single Ag-MCSN phase can therefore endow PMMA cement with combined bioactivity and antibacterial activity while improving its thermal and mechanical performance, a combination that holds promise for infection-resistant bone reconstruction.

papers.title: Engineering Organoid Microenvironments: Advances in Tissue Engineering for Disease Modeling and Drug Development.
papers.abstract: Organoid technology, a fast-developing three-dimensional in vitro culture system, partially reproduces the native tissue architecture, heterogeneous cell composition, and physiological functions of human organs, serving as a versatile tool for disease simulation, drug screening, toxicology testing, regenerative research, and precision therapy. However, conventional self-assembled organoids are restricted by immature tissue function, unstable long-term culture, incomplete tissue hierarchy, and poor experimental reproducibility, which severely impedes their clinical translation. Tissue engineering and bioengineering methodologies have greatly improved the physiological relevance of engineered organoids via multiple tunable microenvironment manipulation strategies. Optimized culture conditions, vascularization strategies, and spatial biofabrication collectively remedy the inherent defects of traditional organoid models, while organ-on-a-chip, multiorgan integrated devices, and artificial intelligence further expand their translational application boundaries. Most published reviews mainly focus on the biological features and application potentials of organoids, whereas few systematically synthesize relevant optimization strategies from an engineering perspective. This review first introduces the basic biological principles of organoid self-organization, then comprehensively summarizes cutting-edge engineering strategies for enhancing organoid maturation. We also elaborate on the translational value of engineered organoids in disease modeling, drug development, and personalized treatment, and discuss key obstacles including standardization, batch consistency, large-scale production, and clinical translation. Different from previous reviews, this paper constructs an engineering-centered analytical framework, providing theoretical references for developing next-generation organoid platforms with superior physiological performance and clinical practicability.

papers.title: Collision Rendering: GPU-Accelerated Trajectory Planning on Sparse Voxel Radiance Fields with Risk-Bounded Collision Checking
papers.abstract: Although radiance fields provide detailed scene representations for robotics, they remain underexplored for trajectory planning, without a widely agreed-upon way to translate learned spatial primitives into reliable collision criteria. To bridge this gap, we introduce Collision Rendering, the first trajectory planning framework on sparse voxel radiance fields (SVR), which supports GPU-accelerated, risk-bounded collision checking and a differentiable collision cost. Our key insight is that the structured volumetric density of SVR allows its rendering pipeline to serve as a fast numerical approximator of collision probability. We approximate the robot with collision spheres and place a coinciding spherical camera at each sphere. Under a probabilistic collision model, we derive an upper bound on each sphere's maximum directional collision probability from the camera's rendering pipeline. Evaluating this bound on the GPU yields a modular collision checker that integrates with established sampling-based planners without an auxiliary geometric map or changes to the learned representation. We further compute a collision cost and its gradients from rendered opacities through the same pipeline, extending the framework to trajectory optimization. Experiments demonstrate millisecond collision checking time on a consumer-grade GPU and collision-free trajectories in all queries, outperforming other radiance field-based planners.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Global Sensitivity Analysis of Patient-Specific Coronary Hemodynamics Under Unsteady Flow Conditions
papers.abstract: Patient-specific computational models of the coronary arteries demonstrate transformative potential for physiological assessment, identifying hemodynamic markers associated with disease progression, and optimizing treatment. Unfortunately, these models rarely account for input parameter uncertainty, limiting confidence in predictions and their clinical interpretation. Herein, we present a novel uncertainty quantification-finite element framework that integrates computationally efficient techniques to characterize and propagate uncertainty through patient-specific coronary simulations under unsteady flow conditions. Principal component analysis characterized variability in pulsatile coronary velocity waveforms, while uncertainty in blood pressure, viscosity, density, and heart rate is represented through probability distributions. Polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) enabled efficient uncertainty propagation and global sensitivity analysis across three patient-specific models, quantifying variability in time-averaged wall shear stress (WSS), oscillatory shear index, and cross-flow index. Fourth-order PCE emulators converged across all three patients, yielding analyses of 505 models per patient, with median coefficients of variation ranging from 0.15-0.20 for time-averaged WSS, 0.54-0.75 for oscillatory shear index, and 0.28-0.38 for cross-flow index, highlighting greater relative uncertainty in multidirectional WSS metrics. Global sensitivity analysis revealed that time-averaged WSS variability was governed by the individual effects of velocity and blood viscosity, with parameter interactions contributing <2% of total variance. In contrast, velocity waveform uncertainty dominated variability in the oscillatory shear index and cross-flow index, with higher-order parameter interactions accounting for 20.7-34.5% and 26.6-37.8% of total variance, respectively.

papers.title: One Phase Is Enough: Sim-to-Real Transfer with Direct Visual Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Sim-to-real reinforcement learning (RL) has enabled impressive robotic behaviors, yet deploying policies directly from vision remains challenging. A common approach first trains a teacher policy with RL using privileged state observations, then distills its behavior into a vision-based student via imitation. However, the resulting student can substantially underperform its teacher. Directly training visual policies with RL offers a promising alternative, but learning task-relevant visual representations from scratch can be sample-inefficient, making one-phase visual RL intractable. We propose DRIFT, a simple recipe for efficient one-phase visual RL using image observations available at test time. Our key insight is to use frozen, pretrained foundation vision encoders, allowing RL to focus on learning control from existing visual representations. Freezing the encoder avoids costly backpropagation through the vision backbone, while its pretrained representations enable real-world transfer from fast, rasterized simulation rendering. Under matched architectures, observations, and compute budgets, DRIFT outperforms two-phase distillation and achieves a 58.8% relative improvement in average real-world success rate across three manipulation tasks. Controlled simulation evaluations demonstrate that DRIFT's relative advantage grows from roughly 9% in-distribution to over 61% under out-of-distribution shifts, suggesting that stronger generalization contributes to superior real-world transfer. Project website: https://jmarangola.github.io/one-phase-visual-rl/

papers.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a $\underline{D}\text{istributed}$ $\underline{S}\text{ampling-based}$ $\underline{T}\text{rajectory}$ $\underline{O}\text{ptimization} \ \text{(DS-TO)}$ architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to both the constraint-induced non-convexity and the decisions of other agents. The resulting algorithm is fully decentralized, requiring only neighborhood communication, with all local updates executed in parallel across agents. Efficient variations, including parallel Jacobi updates within each agent's subproblem and single-step constraint linearization, further reduce computation. Experiments on 2D and 3D tasks with up to 1024 agents demonstrate improved exploration and constraint satisfaction over state-of-the-art derivative-based distributed optimization, and superior scalability to existing distributed sampling methods.

papers.title: Neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional phonon Boltzmann-Fourier coupling for multiscale heat transport in silicon fin arrays
papers.abstract: Localized heating in semiconductor devices can produce non-diffusive phonon transport near heat-generating regions, while heat spreading through the surrounding substrate remains well described by Fourier conduction. We present a hybrid framework that couples a pretrained neural operator for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) within individual fins to a Fourier model of a shared substrate. To reduce the cost of repeated BTE solves across fin positions and coupling iterations, a DeepONet maps each fin's substrate-interface temperature and heating state to its temperature and heat-flux fields. The operator is trained on interface temperatures generated by a linearized proxy of the coupled problem, which avoids explicit training data collection from full coupled runs. An energy-balance penalty regularizes the learned operator, and a mixed finite-element formulation represents substrate heat flux in an H(div)-conforming space. The two models exchange temperature and normal heat flux through a non-overlapping Schwarz iteration with adaptive Aitken relaxation. We evaluate the framework on an idealized three-dimensional array of 100 silicon fins. For a held-out switching configuration, the neural-operator-Fourier solution differs from the direct BTE-Fourier reference by a maximum of 0.3 K in temperature and 0.6% in relative flux across all fins. Excluding the one-time substrate factorization, the coupled surrogate run takes about 50 s, compared with 2 h 28 min for direct coupling, a speedup of approximately 180x. Additional held-out switching patterns converge with the same trained operator. These results demonstrate neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional kinetic-continuum coupling for the tested geometry and material. This bidirectional strategy may extend to other multiscale materials problems coupling learned local neural models with continuum solvers.

papers.title: Diagnosing Epistemic Uncertainty in Neural Operators: Effects of Initialization, Discretization, and Function Sampling
papers.abstract: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for mappings between function spaces, but their reliability cannot be characterized by the performance of a single trained model. Existing neural operator uncertainty quantification approaches often characterize predictive uncertainty without separately identifying the contributions of individual sources of epistemic uncertainty. Finite sampling of the training function space, output discretization, and model initialization can produce substantial variation among learned operators even when the underlying physical problem is deterministic. We systematically investigate these sources of epistemic uncertainty across a diverse set of operator learning architectures. Across our experiments, we train approximately 46,000 neural operator models and construct ensembles over training datasets, model initializations, and output discretizations to characterize distributions of relative $L_2$ error rather than individual trained realizations. We find substantial architecture-dependent differences in epistemic uncertainty, with model initialization often accounting for the largest proportion of variance in relative $L_2$ error. The ranked performance of neural operator architectures can invert as the number and spatial distribution of output samples change, with the best architectures under sparse or randomly sampled observations differing from those at higher-resolution or structured discretizations. Furthermore, ensembles that reliably characterize aggregate operator error can provide unreliable estimates of error quantiles for individual test functions. These results highlight the importance of distinguishing the sources of epistemic uncertainty when evaluating neural operator reliability and establishing robust benchmarking practices.

papers.title: CaLA: Causal Latent Adjustment for World Models under Adaptive Policies
papers.abstract: World models is answering ``imagine" answers to ``what-if'' questions via imagined rollouts. But rollouts collected by adaptive policies induce treatment-outcome confounding in imagined rollouts. We study this problem in Match-3 difficulty adjustment, where latent player skill influences both assigned difficulty and churn. We build a fully specified Match-3 SCM with sequential mechanics, adaptive assignment, and paired ground-truth interventions, on which unadjusted models fit to the logged trajectories select difficulty settings that raise churn. We then introduce Causal Latent Adjustment (CaLA), a DAG-constrained world model that infers a variational player representation from pretreatment history. Across our evaluations, CaLA provides the most reliable population-level intervention estimates and competitive individualized decisions, although rich handcrafted histories can remain advantageous for individual-level adjustment. We further find that residual correction can degrade causal decision quality despite improving predictive fit, highlighting the need to distinguish predictive accuracy, confounding adjustment and the behavior of downstream causal estimators.

papers.title: Successful management of a proximal femoral comminuted fracture occurring after total hip arthroplasty in a small-breed dog
papers.abstract: Medical records of a 7-year-old neutered female Chihuahua were reviewed to describe the management of a proximal femoral comminuted fracture following total hip arthroplasty (THA). The dog underwent staged bilateral THA for hip dysplasia and concurrent orthopedic disease. Twelve days after the second THA, a fall resulted in a Vancouver type B3-like periprosthetic proximal femoral fracture. Revision surgery involved femoral stem replacement and fracture stabilization using an interlocking femoral stem system. Postoperative radiographs showed appropriate implant positioning. Radiographic evidence of bone healing was observed by postoperative day 132. The fracture followed a traumatic event, although the potential contributions of implant-related stress risers and femoral preparation could not be determined. This case suggests that interlocking stem revision may be an effective treatment option for periprosthetic femoral fractures in selected small-breed dogs.

The interstory drift ratio and relative vertical displacement were used as complementary demand measures to derive the joint mean damage index. Results identified peak ground acceleration as the dominant factor, followed by concrete strength grade and burial depth effects.

papers.title: Predicting Groundwater Flow and Solute Transport in Coastal Aquifers Using a DeepONet-Based Parametric Surrogate
papers.abstract: Coastal aquifer responses to tides can be simulated using coupled groundwater flow and solute transport models, but repeated numerical simulations are computationally costly. We developed a parametric Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) surrogate for an idealized two-dimensional coastal aquifer simulated with SUTRA. The model maps tidal amplitude and landward hydraulic head to transient pressure head and concentration fields. Supervised, physics-regularized, and physics-only training strategies were compared, and the supervised model was evaluated at higher tidal amplitudes using few shot adaptation. On test simulations within source-range, the supervised model achieved pooled RMSEs of 5.87×10−3 m for pressure head and 5.75×10−4 for concentration. Adding continuous physics constraints did not improve agreement with the numerical reference, and lower physics residuals did not necessarily correspond to smaller field errors. Prediction accuracy decreased outside the source range, whereas adaptation with two higher-amplitude simulations reduced pressure-head and concentration RMSEs by 36.8% and 68.5%, respectively. The surrogate reconstructed a complete 72-h response in approximately 0.018 s, compared with approximately 9.09 s for the numerical simulation. These results demonstrate the potential of DeepONet as a computationally efficient surrogate for tide-driven coastal aquifer simulations while showing the dependence of physics-based regularization and adaptation on training data and forcing-space coverage.

papers.title: Interface engineering in hybrid supercapacitors using conductive polymers and two-dimensional nanomaterials: recent progress and future perspectives
papers.abstract: The use of conductive polymers and two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials has led to a new generation of supercapacitor electrodes that are capable of delivering exceptional performance. Conductive polymers (CPs) are known to deliver excellent pseudocapacitance due to redox reactions at the electrode surface and have been found to be highly versatile as they may be designed using synthetic chemistry. However, conductive polymers are often subject to problems associated with volume expansion during charge/discharge cycles, mechanical degradation through cracking or exfoliation of the film and poor cyclic durability over extended periods. Graphene-derived materials, MXenes and transition metal-dichalcogenide-based nanosheets possess extremely large surface areas, provide a very low electrical resistance path and rapid ion-transport channels; however, despite these attractive features, there are several reasons why they do not always reach their full potential. These include a tendency for the nanosheets to form stacks and the relatively inaccessible nature of many of the active sites within them. Hybridization is recognized as an efficient method to overcome both of these constraints; however, the ability to enhance the electrochemical response of hybrids depends almost exclusively upon the quality of the interface between the different constituent parts, rather than being solely determined by the combination of each component. As a result, this mini-review will focus specifically on interface engineering in hybrid conductive polymer/2D material-based supercapacitors with an emphasis on electrostatic attraction, chemical bonding, π–π stacking, hydrogen bonding, hierarchical porosity and structural engineering of heterojunctions. The impact of each of these methods on electron transfer, ion diffusion, mechanical strength, cycling rate and cyclic durability will be extensively examined. Examples of recent hybrid architectures will then be directly compared to establish developing correlations between the interface-structure and overall device performance. A number of current challenges remain in terms of swelling of polymeric films, delamination of interfaces, restacking of nanosheets, scaling-up hybrid devices and lack of understanding of dynamic interfaces. Future possibilities in terms of operando characterization, AI-driven design of hybrid structures, digital twin representations of hybrid devices, self-healing interfaces, printable electrodes, flexible and microsupercapacitors will be described. Ultimately, it is anticipated that establishing a clear relationship between the interface and resultant transport behavior will facilitate the rationally designed creation of stable and practical next-generation hybrid supercapacitors.

papers.title: When behaviour remembers: Fractional-order HIV transmission dynamics with risk switching, delayed diagnosis, and viral suppression
papers.abstract: HIV transmission is governed by the interplay of biological progression, behavioural heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, treatment history, and persistent epidemiological effects. Classical integer-order compartmental models are inherently memoryless and may therefore provide an incomplete description of transmission processes in which past states influence current epidemic dynamics. This study develops a behaviourally structured fractional-order HIV/AIDS model that integrates risk heterogeneity, behavioural switching, infection progression, diagnosis, treatment failure, and viral suppression within a unified dynamical system. The population is structured into high- and low-risk susceptible classes together with exposed, undiagnosed infectious, diagnosed infectious, treated unsuppressed, virally suppressed, and AIDS classes. Epidemiological memory is incorporated through the Caputo–Fabrizio fractional derivative with a nonsingular fading-memory kernel. The model is shown to be biologically well posed through positivity and boundedness of solutions, and the disease-free and endemic equilibria are characterized analytically. Using the next-generation operator, a biologically interpretable basic reproduction number is derived as an invasion threshold for disease persistence. Stability analysis establishes the dynamical behaviour of the equilibria in relation to this threshold, while normalized sensitivity analysis identifies parameters with the strongest local influence on transmission. Numerical simulations illustrate that the fractional order can substantially modify epidemic transients and long-term trajectories, while behavioural switching, diagnosis, treatment initiation, treatment failure, and viral suppression jointly reshape the modelled transmission potential. Benchmark intervention scenarios further show that reductions in effective infectious contact, accelerated diagnosis, increased treatment uptake, and sustained viral suppression can reduce the modelled reproduction number and infectious burden, with the magnitude of these effects depending on the adopted parameterization. The results provide a mathematical framework for examining how behavioural heterogeneity, treatment pathways, and epidemiological memory interact in a modelled HIV epidemic. The intervention findings should be interpreted as deterministic, model-based scenarios and mechanistic hypotheses rather than as population-specific predictions of HIV-control effectiveness. Their generalizability requires empirical calibration, uncertainty quantification, and validation against longitudinal epidemiological and treatment data.

papers.title: Accelerating MOF discovery for CO 2 capture: End‐to‐end molecular‐to‐process framework via two‐stage active learning
papers.abstract: The discrepancy between intrinsic material properties and macroscopic process performance hinders the efficient screening of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for carbon capture. In this work, we propose a molecular‐to‐process screening framework integrating high‐throughput molecular simulation, rigorous pressure swing adsorption (PSA) process optimization, and machine learning. A pivotal advancement is our end‐to‐end deep learning surrogate, which predicts process‐level metrics directly from MOF crystallographic information. Additionally, to accelerate the discovery of superior candidates, we implement a two‐stage active learning strategy with an adaptive mechanism, mitigating the adverse effect of domain shift between the initial training set and the vast target library. Applying this framework to 50,921 MOFs, only approximately 1% of the target library is evaluated by high‐fidelity simulations, identifying 55 promising candidates with predicted Pareto dominance over the benchmark CALF‐20. Furthermore, feature importance analysis reveals that accessible surface area, framework density, and N 2 affinity constant are the dominant determinants for PSA performance.

papers.title: Text2Meta: A Staged Language‐to‐Structure Pipeline for Physically Grounded Design of Graded Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) Mechanical Metamaterials
papers.abstract: Mechanical metamaterials enable task‐specific regulation of mechanical behavior through structural architecture. However, a fundamental gap still remains between high‐level human intent and design‐actionable mechanical targets. Existing inverse design frameworks typically assume that such targets are pre‐defined and valid, bypassing the ambiguity of translating functional requirements into physical specifications. Here, we propose Text2Meta, a staged language‐to‐structure pipeline that formalizes requirement translation within the design process. Rather than directly mapping text to geometry, Text2Meta stabilizes linguistic intent into standardized semantics, translates these into mechanically verifiable stress–strain targets, and executes inverse structural synthesis on this physically grounded foundation. The pipeline is instantiated and validated on graded triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) architectures under uniaxial compressive loading, and this staged formulation achieves close agreement between prescribed and realized mechanical behaviors in all three gait regions examined. As a system‐level demonstration, we use Text2Meta to generate regionally graded architectures for humanoid robotic soles, where regional functional descriptions are translated into task‐specific structures that mitigate impact transmission and reduce peak joint torque under dynamic gait loading. These results demonstrate Text2Meta as a physically grounded approach for requirement formalization in graded TPMS metamaterial design, which is in principle extensible to broader architected‐material families.

papers.title: Preview-based trajectory tracking control for intelligent vehicles
papers.abstract: Trajectory tracking control is a fundamental technology in intelligent vehicle autonomous driving systems, directly affecting driving safety and tracking accuracy. To address the limitations of conventional Model Predictive Control (MPC) in terms of computational efficiency under complex driving conditions, as well as the limited constraint-handling capability of the Iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR) and the risks of trajectory lag and boundary violations on low-adhesion roads, this study proposes an iLQR-MPC control strategy with preview-based control. Firstly, a two-degree-of-freedom vehicle dynamics model and a preview-based tracking error model are established to accurately characterize the vehicle dynamic response and future trajectory deviations. Secondly, an iLQR-MPC control framework incorporating preview control is developed. By exploiting the fast iterative convergence of iLQR, an initial control sequence is generated for the MPC optimization, thereby reducing the computational burden of online optimization while retaining MPC’s capability to explicitly handle system constraints. Meanwhile, the preview module evaluates the road curvature and distance to the road boundaries to anticipate upcoming road geometry and safety constraints, enabling proactive control adjustments. Finally, the proposed strategy is validated through co-simulation using MATLAB/Simulink and CarSim, with comparisons against a centerline-based preview strategy and a conventional non-preview control strategy. The results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly reduces trajectory tracking errors while maintaining favorable stability and robustness under challenging conditions, including low-friction road surfaces and high-speed cornering.

papers.abstract: The ability to recognize and use punctuation marks is one of the fundamental skills in learning Bahasa Indonesia in the lower grades. Based on preliminary observations in Class 2.1 of MI IMAMI Kepanjen, some students still had difficulty distinguishing types of punctuation marks, understanding their functions, and determining the appropriate punctuation mark in simple sentences. In addition, learning that was dominated by explanations and written exercises caused some students to be less active and enthusiastic. This study aimed to improve students’ ability to recognize punctuation marks through the application of the Active Learning method assisted by the Punctuation Clothesline Game (“Jemur Baju Tanda Baca”) media. The study employed Classroom Action Research (CAR), carried out in the stages of planning, action implementation, observation, and reflection. Data were collected through observation, tests, interviews, and documentation. The data were analyzed by comparing students’ learning outcomes in the pre-cycle, cycle I, and cycle II. The Punctuation Clothesline Game media was implemented through activities in which students selected and matched punctuation marks with appropriate sentences, so that they were actively involved in learning. Based on the evaluation data, the students’ average score increased from 70 in the pre-cycle to 85 in cycle I and 90 in cycle II. The percentage of learning mastery also increased from 70% to 85% in cycle I and 90% in cycle II. These results show that the application of the Active Learning method assisted by the Punctuation Clothesline Game media can improve students’ ability to recognize punctuation marks. This media also makes learning Bahasa Indonesia more active, engaging, and enjoyable. Thus, this method can serve as an alternative for teaching punctuation to lower-grade students in madrasah ibtidaiyah (Islamic elementary schools).

summary_en.motivation: The study addresses lower-grade students' difficulties in distinguishing and correctly applying punctuation marks in Bahasa Indonesia.
summary_en.method: A classroom action research design was implemented across planning, action, observation, and reflection cycles using an active-learning approach supported by a punctuation-matching game medium.
summary_en.result: Average scores rose from 70 in the pre-cycle to 90 in cycle II, with mastery increasing from 70% to 90%.
summary_en.validation: Learning outcomes were compared across pre-cycle and two intervention cycles using observation, tests, interviews, and documentation.
